steps.message: Standards Engineering needs the witness-test scope and scheduling package for the municipal arrays that need one, and the list of arrays the System Operations Center can be asked to release as the record stands at 07/14/2025, before the 08/15/2025 League response. The batch is covered by the municipal commissioning checklists, Checklist_Cravenwood_High.pdf through Checklist_Tresbay_Community_Center.pdf, and by the DER Program's commissioning records, including the Program Office's case tracking and its commissioning wiki. Establish which arrays are still in scope for the batch on that date. For each array in scope, determine whether the inverter or power conversion equipment actually installed there is carried on the current Certified Equipment List, and issue the package: for each array that is not carried, the tests to be performed and their basis, who performs and witnesses them, and what has to be on file first. The waiver disposition itself stays with Standards Engineering and is not yours to make. Log a scheduling item in the case tracking for each array that is not carried, record the batch determination on the case, and close the case once the arrays named in the package and the scheduling items standing on it agree. Return your work as a single Word document named Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx, filed in the Program Office's municipal commissioning folder in the document store, giving each determination with the basis you relied on, and the call made one way or the other on carriage.

ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office Page 1
ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1. The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2. Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3. Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4. Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.
Alleniom Utilities · DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com

The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.
§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.
Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.
§4.3  Documentation.
The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
include, at minimum:

the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;

for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
by the Standards Engineer of record;


for witness-tested facilities, the witness engineer’s test record, including instrument identifiers,
measured values, pass/fail dispositions per test point, and the witness engineer’s signature and
date;

the manufacturer’s certificate of conformance, factory test report, or equivalent evidence supporting
the CEL listing relied upon;


Introduced Category 1/2/3 protective-equipment table.\\nRev 3\\n12/01/2021\\nProgram-scope threshold set at 500 kW; added §3.4 aggregation.\\nRev 4\\n03/01/2024\\nAdded §3.5 shared-POI eligibility; added §3.6 controlled-capacity recognition (UL 1741 / UL\\n3141 PCS + Control Narrative); §7 restated to require withdrawal and reapplication for\\npost-execution capacity or POI changes; Table 5-1 rewritten by category.\\n§1 Purpose and Scope\\nThis standard establishes the technical and procedural requirements for interconnection of distributed energy\\nresources (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. It is based on IEEE 1547-2018 and applicable state\\ninterconnection rules filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC), and it applies to all DER classes\\ndefined in §3.\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 governs:\\n classification of DER facilities by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling (§3);\\n eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);\\n recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);\\n protective and control equipment requirements by class and category (§5);\\n\\n\\n---\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard Page 2\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024\\n treatment of post-execution changes to executed interconnection service agreements (§7).\\nThis standard is read together with the APUC-filed interconnection tariff (§12). Where a topic is addressed by both\\nthis standard and the tariff, the tariff controls. Requirements for real-time monitoring and communications integration\\nare established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.\\n§2 References\\nThe following documents are referenced within this standard. Unless otherwise noted, the latest published revision\\napplies.\\n IEEE 1547-2018 — IEEE Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources\\nwith Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.\\n DPS-07 Rev 2 — Alleniom Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023). Establishes distribution\\nprotection requirements including protective devices at points of interconnection with export-capable in-scope\\nfacilities.\\n TCS-02 — Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021). Governs utility-owned RTU\\ninstallation and SCADA telemetry for DER at and above the program-scope threshold; establishes the condition\\nfor permission to operate.\\n CEL-2025-Q2 — Alleniom Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025). Listing basis: UL 1741-SB and UL\\n3141. The CEL front matter restates §3.6 of this standard.\\n ERP-9 — Alleniom Engineering Referral Procedure (Form ER-11). §3 routes any standards \\n§3 DER Classification\\nDER facilities are classified by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling, in accordance with\\nIEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.\\nCommercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW; medium-scale 1 MW–5 MW; program scope ≥500 kW; sub-500 kW DER\\n(commercial and residential) is handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process, outside the DER Program.\\nDefinitions of terms used in this standard follow IEEE 1547-2018 and, where applicable, the definitions in the\\nAPUC-filed tariff. The terms aggregate nameplate capacity and point of common coupling (PCC) have the meanings\\nassigned by IEEE 1547-2018 and reflected in Company practice. The terms point of interconnection (POI),\\nexport-capable, and pure-generation site are used in accordance with their ordinary meaning in utility\\ninterconnection practice.\\n\\n---\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard\\nPage 3\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024\\nTable 3-1 — DER classes\\nClass\\nAggregate\\nnameplate at PCC\\nProgram status\\nReview path\\nProtective\\nequipment\\nreference\\nResidential / small\\ncommercial\\n< 500 kW\\nSimplified Small-Systems\\nProcess — outside the\\nDER Program\\nSimplified small-systems\\nscreening\\nTable 5-1, Category\\n1\\nCommercial small-scale\\n500 kW – 1 MW\\nIn DER Program scope\\nInitial screening +\\nsupplemental review under\\nSRP-3\\nTable 5-1, Category\\n2\\nMedium-scale\\n1 MW – 5 MW\\nIn DER Program scope\\nInitial screening + system\\nimpact study\\nTable 5-1, Category\\n3\\nLarge-scale (out of scope\\nfor this standard)\\n> 5 MW\\nHandled under transmissio\\nn-interconnection\\nprocedures\\nFull study process\\nNot addressed\\nThe program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer\\nclass, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.\\n§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity\\nAggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment\\ninterconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets\\ngovern; derated or \\\"operating\\\" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.\\n§3.2 Point of common coupling\\nThe point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's\\ndistribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),\\nthe latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.\\n§3.3 Determination on the basis of application\\nClassification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,\\nand cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and\\nthe address of record govern.\\n§3.4 Aggregation\\nCo-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.\\nPreviously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission\\nto operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form\\nin which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the\\nresulting program-scope determination.\\nAn applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the\\napplication form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,\\nthe existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against\\nthe Company existing-DER register.\\n§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility\\nA new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought\\nto current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the\\nexisting system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its\\nown service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.\\n\\n\\n---\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard\\nPage 4\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024\\nThe two dispositions available under §3.5 are:\\n1.  Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to\\ncurrent monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The\\napplicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where\\nfeasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.\\n2.  Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind\\nthe meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and\\nits own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.\\nClass placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.\\nRetrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the\\napplicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path\\nunder §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.\\n§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition\\nA limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control\\nNarrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the\\nrecognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI\\n32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.\\nRequired submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for\\nprogram-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:\\n1.  A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where\\napplicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the\\nsetpoint range.\\n2.  An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system\\nenforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response\\ntimes, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.\\nThese two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.\\nRecognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.\\nEnforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the\\nrecognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:\\n Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry\\nmonitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation\\ntriggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.\\n POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which\\nno customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per\\nTable 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips\\nthe site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require\\nadditional utility hardware.\\nEnforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does\\nnot reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.\\nNo controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and\\nan approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.\\nCertified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL\\ndoes not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific\\ncertification and Control Narrative are always required.\\n\\n\\n---\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard Page 5\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024\\n§4 Screening and Study Process\\nApplications in DER Program scope proceed through initial technical screening under Interconnection Studies.\\nFacilities not passing initial screens may be evaluated under supplemental review per SRP-3 or advance to a system\\nimpact study. This standard does not restate SRP-3; the daytime minimum-load convention and other screen\\nmethodologies are prescribed there.\\n§5 Protective and Control Equipment\\nProtective equipment requirements are stated by category in Table 5-1, keyed to the classes of §3.\\nTable 5-1 — Protective equipment by category\\nItem Category 1 (< 500 kW) Category 2 (500 kW – 1 MW\\nexport sites)\\nCategory 3 (1 MW – 5 MW\\nexport sites)\\nApplicable class Residential / small\\ncommercial\\nCommercial small-scale Medium-scale\\nDER-side disconnect Required (customer-owned\\nlockable visible-break)\\nRequired (customer-owned\\nlockable visible-break)\\nRequired (customer-owned\\nlockable visible-break)\\nInterconnection protective\\nfunctions (IEEE 1547-2018\\nclause 4)\\nProvided by certified inverterProvided by certified inverter\\nand/or dedicated protection\\nrelay\\nDedicated protection relay\\nrequired\\nDER breaker with protection\\nrelay scheme (for\\nload/generation-decoupling\\narrangements)\\nNot required As specified per site by\\nprotection engineering\\nAs specified per site by\\nprotection engineering\\nPOI recloser (utility-owned)Not required Category 2 export sites —\\nPOI recloser: not required\\nRequired\\nAnti-islanding Certified inverter functions\\nper IEEE 1547-2018\\nCertified inverter functions per\\nIEEE 1547-2018;\\nsupplemented by relay scheme\\nwhere dedicated relay is\\ninstalled\\nDedicated relay scheme with\\ntransfer trip where required by\\nprotection engineering\\nDirectional-power element\\n(ANSI 32) — pure-generation\\nsites\\nNot applicable Set on POI recloser where\\ninstalled; used to enforce a\\n§3.6 controlled limit where\\napplicable\\nSet on POI recloser; used to\\nenforce a §3.6 controlled limit\\nwhere applicable\\nMetering Bidirectional revenue meterBidirectional revenue meterBidirectional revenue meter,\\nprimary or secondary as\\nfeeder configuration requires\\nUtility RTU and SCADA\\ntelemetry\\nNot required Required per TCS-02 (≥500\\nkW)\\nRequired per TCS-02\\nNotes to Table 5-1.\\n1.  Category placement reflects the export configuration prevailing at the site. Where a site's configuration warrants\\nrequirements differing from the tabular default — including, for example, load/generation-decoupling\\narrangements in which generation is isolated by a DER breaker with a dedicated protection relay scheme —\\nprotection engineering may specify the applicable requirements through the Engineering Referral Procedure\\n(ERP-9 §3, Form ER-11).\\n\\n---\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard\\nPage 6\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024\\n2.  Table 5-1 addresses protective and control equipment. Monitoring and communications requirements are\\nestablished under TCS-02.\\n3.  Where §3.6 recognition is in effect at a pure-generation site with a utility POI recloser, the ANSI 32\\ndirectional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips on violation.\\n§6 Monitoring and Control\\nFacilities at or above the TCS-02 program threshold shall provide real-time monitoring and control integration through\\na utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry as prescribed by TCS-02. Live telemetry to the Company system\\noperations center is a condition of permission to operate. This standard does not restate TCS-02; refer to TCS-02 §5\\nfor the telemetry rule and to Alleniom system operations for RTU installation scheduling.\\nSite-level control functions required by §3.6 (Power Control System recognition), by Table 5-1 (dedicated protection\\nrelay schemes, DER breaker arrangements), and by ERP-9 site determinations, together satisfy the\\ncontrol-integration expectations of this section as applied to the specific facility.\\n§7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions\\nPost-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not\\npermitted for capacity or POI changes.\\nScope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by\\nboth parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without\\ninvoking this section.\\nPrincipal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection\\nservice agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as\\nexecuted.\\nRequired path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of\\ninterconnection after ISA execution shall:\\n1.  Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;\\n2.  File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and\\n3.  Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.\\nThe new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested\\nchange is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the\\napplicant as involving new or existing equipment.\\nOther post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within\\nthe same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the\\nchange-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.\\nDownstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment\\nreservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in\\nqueue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application\\nreceives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.\\n§8 Records and Compliance\\nInterconnection Studies retains the application file, executed ISA, and study record for each in-scope facility for the\\nretention period established by Regulatory Affairs. Standards Engineering maintains the current revision of this\\nstandard, the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2 and subsequent editions), and the Engineering Referral\\nProcedure (ERP-9) register of per-site determinations.\\n\\n\\n---\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard\\nPage 7\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024\\nAny conflict between this standard and the APUC-filed tariff is resolved in favor of the tariff. data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":43,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{"success":true,"page":{"id":17,"path":"der-program/correspondence/2025-06-20-aml-escalation-letter","title":"2025-06-20 AML Escalation Letter","description":"Formal escalation letter dated 06/20/2025 from the Alleron Municipal League on behalf of 14 municipalities and school districts with stalled solar projects","content":"# 2025-06-20 AML Escalation Letter\n\nALLERON MUNICIPAL LEAGUE\nThe united voice of Alleron’s cities, towns, and school districts\nRef: AML-2025-0620-DER\nJune 20, 2025\nMs. Dana Whitcomb\nVice President, Distribution Operations\nAlleniom Utilities\nRE: Escalation — DER Interconnection Program Delays Affecting Fourteen Municipalities and School\nDistricts\nDear Ms. Whitcomb:\nOn behalf of the Alleron Municipal League and the fourteen member communities identified below, I write to\nconvey our formal and collective concern regarding the continued and, in our view, unreasonable delays\naffecting commercial-scale solar interconnection projects currently stalled within Alleniom Utilities’ Distributed\nEnergy Resource (DER) interconnection program. This letter follows repeated informal outreach by individual\nmember staff to your DER Program Office over the preceding several months, outreach which has not produced\nthe clarity or the timely progress our members need in order to close out their local capital projects.\nThe League is writing on behalf of 14 municipalities and school districts across the state of Alleron whose\ncommercial-scale solar projects — commissioned in good faith with voter-approved bond proceeds, adopted\ncapital budgets, energy-savings performance contracts, and in several instances state and federal grant awards\nAdditional League members with projects in the same posture have asked to be represented collectively through\nthis correspondence and are prepared to be identified upon request. Every one of these projects has been\nreviewed and approved by the applicable local governing body, financed through public procurement, and\nconstructed by licensed contractors under permits issued by the relevant authority having jurisdiction.\nThe projects at issue are not speculative or exploratory. They range in size from approximately 500 kW to nearly\n1 MW and are installed at public schools, municipal water and wastewater treatment plants, community centers,\npublic libraries, and other municipal facilities. In the great majority of cases construction is complete, mechanical\nand electrical inspections have been closed out by local inspectors, and equipment has been standing\nenergized-ready — in some instances for a period now measured in months — pending only the Company’s\nauthorization to interconnect and place the systems into commercial operation. Each additional month of delay\ndefers budgeted operating savings, extends the payback horizon presented to our members’ councils and school\nboards, and in the case of grant-funded projects places committed public funding at direct risk of forfeiture.\nOur members are patient partners. They understand that the interconnection of distributed generation on the\nCompany’s distribution system requires careful technical review and, at times, coordination with equipment\nprocurement, feeder studies, and protection-scheme confirmation. They are willing to meet reasonable technical\nrequirements. What they are not able to accept — and what this League cannot accept on their behalf — is an\nBrookfen Unified School District\nCity of Elmsworth\nDarnwick Community School District\nLockmere Community School District\nCravenwood Community School District\nTown of Tresbay\nCity of Marden Falls\nTown of Holcott\nremain suspended in your interconnection queue awaiting energization. Among the affected members are:\n812 Larchmont Street · Cordwyn, Alleron 16CW · (651) 555-0244\nHalston, Alleron 01HA\n4200 Veldmere Boulevard\n\n---\n\nextended period of silence, shifting explanations, and open-ended hold status without a clear articulation of what\nis required, by whom, and by when.\nAccordingly, and in a spirit of continued cooperation, the League respectfully requests the following from\nAlleniom Utilities:\n1.  A full accounting of current queue status. For each identified League-member project, please provide the\nproject’s assigned application number, current queue position, and complete processing history to date.\n2.  Hold reasons. For every project currently in a hold, pending, or suspended posture, please identify the\nspecific reason for the hold, the party responsible for the next action, the information or resource required to\nrelease the hold, and the date the hold was established.\n3.  Expected energization dates. For each project, please provide the Company’s current best estimate of the\ndate on which Permission to Operate will be issued, together with any intermediate milestone dates\n(studies, equipment delivery, witness testing, or telemetry acceptance) that inform that estimate.\n4.  A written response. We request the Company’s response in writing, addressed to the undersigned at the\nLeague’s Cordwyn office, within a reasonable period consistent with the urgency our members’ councils\nand school boards are attaching to this matter.\n5.  A meeting. We request an in-person meeting between the Company’s senior distribution leadership, the\nLeague’s executive office, and designated representatives of the affected members, to be scheduled at the\nCompany’s offices in Halston or at a mutually convenient location in Cordwyn at the Company’s preference.\nThe League is prepared to convene our members on short notice once the Company proposes a date.\nFor your awareness, a copy of this letter has been provided to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC),\nEnergy Resources Division, for the Division’s information. The League has taken this step not as a matter of\nconfrontation but out of a good-faith obligation to keep the Commission’s staff apprised of a program-level\nconcern affecting a substantial number of Alleron public entities across multiple service territories within the\nCompany’s distribution footprint. It remains our strong preference to resolve this matter directly with Alleniom\nUtilities.\nThe League and its members recognize that Alleniom Utilities has been a constructive counterparty on many\nprior initiatives, and we approach this escalation with the expectation that the Company shares our interest in\nrestoring predictable, transparent processing timelines to the DER program. Our members’ communities have\ninvested public funds, published expected in-service dates to their constituents, and in several cases entered\ninto contractual arrangements predicated on interconnection occurring by dates that are now past. The credibility\nof local government energy planning across Alleron is meaningfully bound up in the outcome, and we are\nconfident the Company understands the seriousness with which we, our elected officials, and our school boards\nregard it.\nI would be grateful for the courtesy of an acknowledgment of receipt at your earliest convenience, and I remain\navailable to discuss any aspect of the foregoing at the telephone number above. Thank you for your prompt\nattention to this matter.\nRespectfully submitted,\nAlden Pryce\nAlden Pryce\nExecutive Director\nAlleron Municipal League\ncc: Ms. Nia Fairweather, Director, Energy Resources Division, Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC), One\nLeague member managers and superintendents (distribution list on file)\nCapitol Plaza, Suite 900, Cordwyn, Alleron 14CW","content_type":"markdown","editor":"markdown","is_published":true,"is_private":false,"locale":"en","created_at":"2026-11-27T02:27:42.791943+00:00","updated_at":"2026-11-27T02:27:42.791943+00:00","tags":["correspondence","municipal","regulatory"],"author_name":"Alden Pryce","author_email":"alden.pryce@alleronmunicipalleague.org"},"error":""}"}],"structuredContent":{"success":true,"page":{"id":17,"path":"der-program/correspondence/2025-06-20-aml-escalation-letter","title":"2025-06-20 AML Escalation Letter","description":"Formal escalation letter dated 06/20/2025 from the Alleron Municipal League on behalf of 14 municipalities and school districts with stalled solar projects","content":"# 2025-06-20 AML Escalation Letter

this correspondence and are prepared to be identified upon request. Every one of these projects has been

1 MW and are installed at public schools, municipal water and wastewater treatment plants, community centers,
public libraries, and other municipal facilities. In the great majority of cases construction is complete, mechanical
and electrical inspections have been closed out by local inspectors, and equipment has been standing
energized-ready — in some instances for a period now measured in months — pending only the Company’s
authorization to interconnect and place the systems into commercial operation. Each additional month of delay
defers budgeted operating savings, extends the payback horizon presented to our members’ councils and school
boards, and in the case of grant-funded projects places committed public funding at direct risk of forfeiture.
Our members are patient partners. They understand that the interconnection of distributed generation on the
Company’s distribution system requires careful technical review and, at times, coordination with equipment
procurement, feeder studies, and protection-scheme confirmation. They are willing to meet reasonable technical
requirements. What they are not able to accept — and what this League cannot accept on their behalf — is an

concern affecting a substantial number of Alleron public entities across multiple service territories within the
Company’s distribution footprint. It remains our strong preference to resolve this matter directly with Alleniom
Utilities.

prior initiatives, and we approach this escalation with the expectation that the Company shares our interest in
restoring predictable, transparent processing timelines to the DER program. Our members’ communities have
invested public funds, published expected in-service dates to their constituents, and in several cases entered
into contractual arrangements predicated on interconnection occurring by dates that are now past. The credibility
of local government energy planning across Alleron is meaningfully bound up in the outcome, and we are
confident the Company understands the seriousness with which we, our elected officials, and our school boards
regard it.

Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
INTERNAL DIRECTIVE
TO:	Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
DER Program Manager
CC:	Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
Marcus Deele, SCADA/EMS Engineering
FROM:	Dana Whitcomb, VP, Distribution Operations
DATE:	06/27/2025
SUBJECT:	Backlog Review — Commercial DER Interconnection Program
The Alleron Municipal League's letter of 06/20/2025, submitted on behalf of fourteen member municipalities and school districts and copied to the APUC Energy Resources Division, is the trigger. We are not going to litigate its tone. We are going to fix the underlying condition that produced it.
Effective immediately, I am ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. The scope covers the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population — every application currently sitting in the program queue. I want each one accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action.
The following non-negotiable dates govern this work:
1. 08/15/2025 — Formal written response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs owns the response letter. Harriet Ngoyi is the signatory. The response must address the League's five enumerated requests substantively and by project, not in aggregate.
2. 09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. Queue accounting must be complete before we walk into that room. I will not brief the Commission on partial data. If a project's disposition is not final by 09/10/2025, I want the reason documented in the file, not explained at the podium.
Ground rules for every disposition reached in this review:
Every disposition must be tariff-defensible. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, or operating guideline that supports the action. If the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as they are written. Do not shortcut them, and do not extend them beyond what the tariff contemplates.
Where standards or procedural conflicts exist, route them through the established referral process. Do not resolve them informally in the queue.
No interim energization, no political prioritization, and no queue-date inheritance outside of what the tariff and program policy permit.
Reporting cadence. I want weekly progress updates to the VP office, in writing, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025. Format: counts by disposition category, exceptions requiring VP attention, and any item at risk of missing the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates. Meera, Ivo, and Marcus will support the DER Program Manager with the data pulls, study status, and telemetry/equipment inputs their groups own.
Escalate obstacles to me directly. I would rather field a problem on a Tuesday than read about it in a League follow-up letter.
/s/
Dana Whitcomb
Vice President, Distribution Operations
Alleniom Utilities

Alleniom Utilities — Regulatory Affairs
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
TO: DER Program Manager
CC: Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations
Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
FROM: Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
DATE: 07/01/2025
SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking
1. Confirmation of directive
This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
4. Reporting cadence
The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.
Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
5. General provisions
Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as written. Standards or procedural conflicts route through the established referral process; they are not to be resolved informally in the queue. Queue-date treatment must remain within what the tariff and program policy permit.
Regulatory Affairs will coordinate with Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki) on queue and notice records, and with the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham) on study status, on any input required for the League response or the APUC briefing. The DER Program Manager remains the single point of accountability for the queue-cleanup inputs enumerated in §3.
Escalate obstacles to Regulatory Affairs in writing and, where the obstacle bears on the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates, to the VP office concurrently.
/s/
Harriet Ngoyi
Director, Regulatory Affairs
Alleniom Utilities

ALLERON PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION
Energy Resources Division
Docket:  APUC-2025-ER-014
Ref:  ERD-IR-2025-07-014
Date:  07/07/2025
Ms. Harriet Ngoyi
Director, Regulatory Affairs
Alleniom Utilities
Re:  APUC Information Request — Alleniom Utilities DER Interconnection Program Backlog
Docket APUC-2025-ER-014
Dear Ms. Ngoyi:
The Energy Resources Division of the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC) is in receipt of
correspondence from the Alleron Municipal League dated 06/20/2025 (AML Ref:
AML-2025-0620-DER), copied to the Division, escalating on behalf of fourteen member municipalities
and school districts a program-level concern with the current pace of commercial-scale Distributed
Energy Resource (DER) interconnection processing on the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The
League's letter identifies delays affecting projects at public schools, municipal water and wastewater
facilities, community centers, and public libraries across multiple communities within the Company's
service territory, and raises questions regarding queue status, hold posture, and expected energization
timelines that fall within the Division's continuing oversight of the Company's APUC-filed
interconnection tariff.
The Division intends to be in a position to brief the Commission on the matter at the previously
scheduled DER program briefing on 09/10/2025. In advance of that briefing, and to permit the Division
to assess the Company's DER interconnection program on the basis of the Company's own records
rather than the League's characterization, this letter requests the following information from Alleniom
Utilities.
1.  Commercial DER queue accounting.
For the commercial DER interconnection program (i.e., the ≥500 kW program-scope portfolio
administered by the Company's DER Program Office; simplified small-systems process filings are
outside the scope of this request), the Company is requested to provide a complete queue accounting as
of the most recent full week preceding the response date, including at minimum the following,
presented at the individual-application level and separately summarized in totals:
a.  The count and identity of all applications currently in active processing status, together with each
application's assigned application number, applicant name, site, nameplate capacity, filing date,
current processing step, and the study or decision milestone next due.
One Capitol Plaza, Suite 900  ·  Cordwyn, Alleron 14CW  ·  (651) 555-0180  ·  apuc.alleron.gov
Halston, Alleron 01HA
4200 Veldmere Boulevard

---

b.  The count and identity of all applications currently on on-hold, pending-customer,
pending-standards, or suspended status, together with the specific hold reason of record for
each, the party responsible for the next action, the information or resource required to release the
hold, and the date the hold was established.
c.  The count and identity of all applications for which one or more study or processing timelines
established under the Company's filed interconnection tariff, procedures, or executed study
agreements have been exceeded as of the reporting date, together with the timeline of record, the
actual elapsed time, and the current cause of the overrun.
d.  The count and identity of all applications withdrawn — whether by written applicant request, by
application of the tariff's deemed-withdrawal provision, or otherwise — during the twelve
months preceding the reporting date, together with the effective date of each withdrawal and the
recorded basis for it.
e.  The count and identity of all formal Notices of Impending Withdrawal, Notices of
Cancellation, or equivalent written notices issued by the Company to applicants during the
twelve months preceding the reporting date, together with the notice date, the date sent, the
method of service, the response deadline computed under the tariff, and the current disposition
(response received / no response / deemed withdrawn / other).
Where any of the foregoing counts is materially affected by data-integrity items known to the Company
requested to identify those items and provide the counts both as they presently appear in the Company's
queue records and as the Company understands the underlying facts to be.
2.  Backlog-cause summary.
The Company is further requested to provide a written summary describing, in the Company's own
characterization, the principal causes of the current backlog in the commercial DER interconnection
program. The summary should address at a minimum: application volume relative to processing
capacity; the availability and lead time of utility-owned equipment required for energization (including
but not limited to RTU and protection equipment); the status of any internal standards reconciliation
activity affecting screening or protection determinations; the sufficiency of certified-equipment
references relied upon by the Company; the sufficiency of hosting-capacity information made available
to prospective applicants; and any other factors the Company identifies as materially contributing to the
current queue posture. Supporting quantitative material (equipment delivery schedules, staffing
utilization, study cycle times, and the like) is welcome and, where practicable, requested.
3.  Format and timing.
Responses should be provided in writing, addressed to the undersigned at the Division's Cordwyn
office, with electronic copies to the docket. Line-item responses under Item 1 above may be provided
by workbook attachment provided each attachment is unambiguously cross-referenced to the
corresponding item. Responses should be received by the Division sufficiently in advance of the
09/10/2025 briefing to allow the Division adequate review; the Division requests that the Company
provide its response no later than 08/22/2025, and, where any portion of the response cannot be
furnished by that date, that the Company so advise the Division in writing no later than 08/08/2025 with
an explanation and a proposed alternative date.
4.  Continuing dialogue.
(for example, timing differences, reconciliation items, or other known data-quality issues), the Company is

---

This request is issued in the ordinary course of the Division's monitoring of interconnection program
performance under the Company's APUC-filed tariff. The Division has no present view as to the merits
of the underlying matter and takes no position on the specific project-level concerns raised in the
League's 06/20/2025 letter, which remain properly a matter between the League's member entities and
the Company in the first instance. The Division's interest at this stage is limited to the queue accounting
and backlog-cause information described above, together with the Company's plan for restoring
predictable processing to the program. The Division remains available to discuss scope, format, or
timing questions at Company request.
The Division appreciates the Company's continued cooperation and looks forward to the Company's
response.
Sincerely,
Nia Fairweather
Nia Fairweather

 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com

 TCS-02                   Rev 1          06/01/2021          Alleniom Standards Engineering

 Document title: Telemetry & Communications Standard

 Applies to: Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities interconnected to the Alleniom Utilities
 distribution system within the DER Program scope

 Effective date: 06/01/2021

 Approving authority: Manager, Standards Engineering



 §1   PURPOSE
 This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
 telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
 and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
 content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
 DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
 Acquisition (SCADA) system.

 TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
 to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
 functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
 standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
 scope of this document.

 §2   SCOPE
 TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
 nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
 handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.

 TCS-02 applies to:

      a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).
      b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).
      c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
       aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.
      d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
       commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
       capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.

Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering                                            TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021



 Where a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common
 coupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the
 aggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.

 §3   RTU REQUIREMENTS

 §3.1   Ownership and installation
 Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
 installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
 owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
 The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
 service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
 installation drawing.

 §3.2   Approved models
 The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU
 service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power
 plant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the
 utility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).

 §3.3   Functional requirements
 Each RTU shall, at minimum:

       a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station
        instrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.
       b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end
        processors over an approved communications path (§4).
       c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum
        of seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon
        restoration.
       d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
        diagnostic points.
       e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
        SCADA/EMS Engineering only.

 §3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements
 The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation
 drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
 dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
 outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.

 §3.5   Time synchronization
 The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
 time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
 timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.

 §3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification




Telemetry & Communications Standard                        Page 2                                                    TCS-02

[page 3]
Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering                                           TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021



 Prior to the RTU being accepted as commissioned, Alleniom shall perform an end-to-end
 point-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,
 exercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.
 Commissioning of the RTU is a prerequisite to the telemetry condition stated in §5.

 §4   COMMUNICATIONS

 §4.1   Communications transport
 The RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by
 SCADA/EMS Engineering:

      a.   Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or
      b.   Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or
      c.   Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held
       by Alleniom.
 Customer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.
 Where site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for
 interconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.

 §4.2   SCADA protocol
 The RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure
 Authentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration
 parameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —
 shall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.

 §4.3   Availability
 The end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a
 monthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent
 loss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be
 corrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected
 equipment.

 §4.4   Address and IP management
 All IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and
 Alleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate
 connections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration
 record.

 §5   TELEMETRY CONDITION FOR PERMISSION TO OPERATE
 §5.   ≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry.
 This requirement applies to all in-scope DER sites, including aggregated facilities under
 DIS-01 §3.4.

 Live telemetry, for the purposes of §5, means that the RTU installed under §3 is:

      a.   Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;






Telemetry & Communications Standard                       Page 3                                                    TCS-02

[page 4]
Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering                                               TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021



       b.   Communicating with Alleniom SCADA over an approved transport (§4) at the refresh
        cadence required by §6; and
       c.   Presenting all required data points (§6) as valid (not stale, not forced, not flagged
        bad-quality) at the SCADA operator display at the moment Permission to Operate (PTO) is
        issued.
 Compliance with §5 is confirmed by the SOC Shift Supervisor on shift at the time PTO is
 requested. The SOC's confirmation is recorded against the interconnection file. PTO shall not be
 issued to any in-scope DER site until §5 is satisfied.

 §6   DATA POINTS AND REFRESH RATES

 §6.1   Required data points
 Each in-scope DER site shall present, at minimum, the following analog and status points to
 Alleniom SCADA. Where the site's arrangement includes multiple inverter blocks or multiple
 aggregated facilities behind a common POI, values shall be reported both individually per block
 and as a facility total.

 Analog values (per site, and per block where applicable):

 Point                                                                  Units             Sign convention
 Real power, net export at POI                                          kW                Export positive
 Reactive power, net at POI                                             kVAr              Absorbing positive
 POI voltage, per phase                                                 V                 —
 POI current, per phase                                                 A                 —
 Frequency at POI                                                       Hz                —
 Gross generation (per inverter block)                                  kW                Generation positive
 Auxiliary/parasitic load (where separately metered)                    kW                Load positive
 Cumulative energy delivered                                            kWh               Export positive
 Cumulative energy received                                             kWh               Import positive
 Ambient / cabinet temperature (RTU health)                             °C                —

 Status and diagnostic points:
 Point                                        Description
 Site online / offline                        Aggregate operating state of the DER
 Inverter/PCS block status                    Per block: run, standby, fault
 Communications heartbeat                     RTU-to-SCADA path health
 Time-sync quality                            GNSS/NTP discipline status
 Configuration version                        Active RTU configuration identifier
 Alarm summary                                Rolled-up device alarm state

 §6.2   Refresh rates






Telemetry & Communications Standard                         Page 4                                                       TCS-02

[page 5]
Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering                                           TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021



 Analog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3
 Class 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than
 every sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an
 integrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be
 reported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.

 §6.3   Data quality
 Every value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,
 restart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the
 RTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be
 reported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.

 §6.4   Retention
 Alleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six
 (36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,
 engineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.

 §7   CYBERSECURITY

 §7.1   Applicability
 The RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any
 customer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this
 section. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security
 program consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.

 §7.2   Access control
 Local and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to
 Alleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication
 against Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are
 managed by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.

 §7.3   Communications security
 DNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All
 communications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an
 Alleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates
 shall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.

 §7.4   Firmware, configuration, and change management
 RTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following
 the Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a
 cryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or
 reconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.

 §7.5   Logging and monitoring
 The RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,
 and firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.
 Anomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response
 procedure.



Telemetry & Communications Standard                       Page 5                                                    TCS-02

[page 6]
Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering                                             TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021



 §7.6   Physical security
 The RTU shall be housed in a locked, tamper-evident enclosure. Enclosure keys, cores, and any
 physical access tokens are held by Alleniom. Physical intrusion of the enclosure shall generate a
 status point (tamper alarm) reported to SCADA under §6.

 §7.7   Incident response
 The customer shall report, without delay, any known or suspected compromise of the RTU, its
 enclosure, its communications transport, or any interface between customer equipment and
 utility-owned telemetry equipment. Reports shall be directed to the Alleniom SOC and to
 SCADA/EMS Engineering.

 §7.8   Decommissioning
 At end of life, the RTU and its cryptographic material are returned to Alleniom for secure disposal.
 Customer equipment previously interfaced to the RTU shall be sanitized of any Alleniom-provided
 credentials before it is repurposed or disposed of.



 End of TCS-02.
