 ALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING
 DISTRIBUTION PROTECTION STANDARD

 Doc no.            Rev           Date                 Owner

 DPS-07             Rev 2         09/15/2023           Alleniom Standards Engineering

 Effective date: 09/15/2023
 Supersedes: DPS-07 Rev 1 (11/04/2019)
 Classification: Engineering Standard — Distribution Protection
 Approved by: Manager, Standards Engineering


 1. PURPOSE
 DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
 (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
 clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
 utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
 the distribution network.
 This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
 devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
 Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
 projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.

 2. SCOPE
 This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
 territory, including but not limited to:
   1.  Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
   2.  Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
   3.  Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
       the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
 Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
 standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
 apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
 Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
 operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
 guidance.

 3. REFERENCES
 The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
      IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
       Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
      IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
      IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
       Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
      ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.


DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023                                                         Page 1

[page 2]
      Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.
      Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.
 Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
 determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.



 4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS

 4.1 General
 Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
 sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
   (a)  Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
       reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
   (b)  Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
       the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
       standard.
   (c)  Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
       between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
   (d)  Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
       cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
       tripping of either.

 4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
 Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
 (POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
 The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
   1.  Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
       current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
       operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
       conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
       backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
   2.  Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
       interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
       Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
   3.  Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
       with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
       —    50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
       —    27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
       —    81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
       —    25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
       —    32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
           backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
       —    79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.
   4.  Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the
       control cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of
       communications shall not defeat local protection.



DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023                                                              Page 2

[page 3]
   5.  Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect
       operable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of
       clearance holds.
   6.  Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location
       accessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer
       premises.

 4.3 DER-Side Protection
 DER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection
 protection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI
 recloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.
 DER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.

 4.4 Grounding
 The DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with
 the grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's
 grounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.

 4.5 Anti-Islanding
 The DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone
 requirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage
 and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive
 scheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;
 otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.

 5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS

 5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing
 The POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:
   (a)  The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream
       recloser.
   (b)  The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per
       the site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the
       site's operating procedure.
   (c)  Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study
       prior to energization.

 5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection
 DER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent
 reasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the
 POI recloser shall trip as backup protection.

 5.3 Direct Transfer Trip
 Direct transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable
 non-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening
 of the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications
 channel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.

 5.4 Reclosing Blocking
 Automatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the
 DER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the

 affected feeder warrants such a change. The determination shall be made per site by Distribution Protection
 Engineering and recorded in the site's interconnection file.
 5.5 Settings Governance
 All protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the
 DER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in
 the field without a written revision order.

 6. TESTING

 6.1 Factory Acceptance
 The POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard
 test protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to
 shipment.

 6.2 Site Acceptance
 Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed
 by Alleniom Utilities:
   1.  Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.
   2.  Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.
   3.  Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,
       and reset.
   4.  End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.
   5.  Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.
   6.  Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.
   7.  Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.

 6.3 Commissioning and Cutover
 Cutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and
 accepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system
 operator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.

 6.4 Periodic Testing
 The POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. DER-side protective
 devices shall be tested by the DER owner on a schedule not to exceed that of comparable utility-owned
 equipment, with test records made available to Alleniom Utilities on request.

 6.5 Post-Event Testing
 Following any operation of the POI recloser attributable to a system disturbance, a DER-side event, or a
 mis-operation, Distribution Protection Engineering shall review the event records and direct such retesting or
 resetting as it determines appropriate before the site is returned to service.

 Distribution Protection Engineering; Distribution Operations; DER Program Office; APUC filing (informational).

 ALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING
 DISTRIBUTION PROTECTION STANDARD

 Doc no.            Rev           Date                 Owner

 DPS-07             Rev 2         09/15/2023           Alleniom Standards Engineering

 Effective date: 09/15/2023
 Supersedes: DPS-07 Rev 1 (11/04/2019)
 Classification: Engineering Standard — Distribution Protection
 Approved by: Manager, Standards Engineering


 1. PURPOSE
 DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
 (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
 clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
 utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
 the distribution network.
 This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
 devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
 Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
 projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.

 2. SCOPE
 This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
 territory, including but not limited to:
   1.  Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
   2.  Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
   3.  Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
       the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
 Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
 standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
 apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
 Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
 operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
 guidance.

 3. REFERENCES
 The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
      IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
       Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
      IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
      IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
       Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
      ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.


DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023                                                         Page 1

[page 2]
      Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.
      Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.
 Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
 determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.



 4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS

 4.1 General
 Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
 sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
   (a)  Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
       reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
   (b)  Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
       the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
       standard.
   (c)  Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
       between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
   (d)  Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
       cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
       tripping of either.

 4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
 Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
 (POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
 The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
   1.  Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
       current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
       operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
       conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
       backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
   2.  Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
       interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
       Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
   3.  Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
       with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
       —    50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
       —    27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
       —    81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
       —    25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
       —    32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
           backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,

 §12.3 Application Intake and Queue Position
 A complete application shall establish the applicant's queue position as of the date the Company
 determines the application to be complete. Applications determined to be incomplete shall be
 returned with a written deficiency notice identifying each item requiring cure and the date by which
 cure is required. Queue position is not transferable between applications except as expressly
 provided in the DER Interconnection Standard.

 §12.4 Deemed Withdrawal Following Notice of Impending Withdrawal or Cancellation
 Upon issuance of a formal written Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation by the
 Company, the applicant shall have thirty (30) business days from the date of the notice to submit
 a substantive response curing the matter identified therein. If the applicant fails to respond within
 thirty (30) business days, the application shall be deemed withdrawn and shall be closed from the
 active queue without further action of the Company.

 legal public holidays observed within the response window. Without limitation, the following

 verified electronic delivery) and shall state the date of issuance, the response deadline computed
 under this section, and the consequence of non-response. The Company shall maintain a log of all
 notices issued, dates of service, and dispositions.

 §12.5 Construction-Payment Defaults
 Where a construction work order or interconnection facilities invoice becomes payable and the
 customer has not remitted the amount due, the Company shall inform the customer in writing of
 the outstanding balance and shall issue a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days from
 the date of that written notice.

 For so long as the thirty (30) business-day payment deadline is running, the affected project shall
 remain on hold in the queue and shall NOT be deemed withdrawn. The construction-payment
 default procedure under this §12.5 is distinct from, and shall not be conflated with, the
 deemed-withdrawal procedure under §12.4; the two mechanisms have different triggers, different
 consequences, and different cure paths.

 Upon receipt of full payment prior to expiration of the deadline, the Company shall promptly
 release the hold and resume the affected work in queue order. If the deadline expires without
 payment, the Company may pursue such remedies as are available under the applicable
 Interconnection Service Agreement and this tariff, including, as a separate and subsequent step,
 issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §12.4.

 terms require withdrawal of the affected application and re-application in accordance with the DER
 Interconnection Standard.

 Applications shall be processed by the Company in queue order on a nondiscriminatory basis.
 No applicant shall be advanced or disadvantaged in the processing sequence by reason of
 identity, affiliation, customer class, geography, or any other factor not expressly provided for in this
 tariff or in the DER Interconnection Standard.

 Scope note. This §12.7 applies to APPLICATION PROCESSING only — that is, to the

 determinations. Utility construction sequencing and the scheduling and allocation of constrained
 utility-owned equipment (including, without limitation, remote terminal units,

 prioritization criteria applicable to constrained equipment. Nothing in this §12.7 shall be construed
 to require the Company to sequence construction or equipment deployment in queue order where
 OG-17 or another operating guideline provides a different criticality-based ordering.

OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline Page 1
ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DISTRIBUTION OPERATIONS
EQUIPMENT DEPLOYMENT PRIORITIZATION
GUIDELINE
Doc no. Rev Effective Date Owner
OG-17 Rev 1 04/07/2025 Alleniom Distribution
Operations
Document Control
Supersedes: none (initial issue).
Review cycle: annual, or on material change to supplier lead times or operating criticality categories.
Approving authority: VP, Distribution Operations.
Distribution: DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; DER Planning Group; System Operations Center
(SOC); Standards Engineering; Supply Chain — Distribution Equipment.
§1  SCOPE
This guideline governs deployment sequencing of constrained utility equipment (RTUs, reclosers) across
completed sites awaiting energization. It applies to Alleniom-owned devices installed by Distribution
Operations for the purpose of energizing a construction-complete distributed energy resource (DER) site,
when supplier lead times or quarterly delivery quantities constrain the number of sites that can be
equipped in a given deployment window.
This guideline does NOT apply to application processing. Nondiscriminatory queue-order treatment of
interconnection applications is governed by Interconnection Tariff §12.7 and by the procedures
administered by Interconnection Studies; nothing in this guideline modifies, displaces, or supplements
those procedures. The rankings established under §2 operate solely on sites for which interconnection
application processing is complete, the interconnection agreement (where required) is executed, and
construction is certified complete by the customer or its contractor.
Devices out of scope: customer-owned protective equipment; utility-owned equipment already installed at
the site; distribution-system reinforcement equipment scheduled under an approved capital work order.
Program scope for the underlying DER remains as defined in DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 and Interconnection Tariff
§12.2.
§2  COMMISSIONING CRITICALITY
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA
As a general rule, deployment priority for constrained equipment follows interconnection queue order,
consistent with the nondiscriminatory treatment principles of Interconnection Tariff §12.7.
A site may be advanced ahead of queue order under certain circumstances — the urgent nature of a
request, in particular for public infrastructure (schools, hospitals, water/wastewater facilities), or an
expedited deployment pathway on reasonable customer request — but only where substantiated by the
site's own recorded attributes (per §3), in order of priority: (1) essential-service function (water/wastewater,
emergency, health); (2) committed in-service or grant-funding deadline; (3) construction-complete date.
Among sites of the same critical nature, the deciding factor is interconnection queue order; requests not
substantiated by these attributes remain in queue order.

---

OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline
Page 2
Factor definitions:
 Essential-service function. A site whose primary served load is a public water or wastewater facility;
a hospital, emergency-response, or first-responder facility; or a public-health facility for which loss of
service is treated as an emergency by the responsible jurisdiction. Essential-service status is
evidenced by the customer's facility classification of record and, where applicable, the served-load
designation on the interconnection application.
 Committed in-service or grant-funding deadline. A contractually committed in-service date, or a
date on which grant funding lapses if the site is not in service, established in a fully executed written
instrument between the customer and a governmental funder, project sponsor, or off-taker. Internal
customer construction targets, marketing dates, budget-cycle expectations, and school-year,
fiscal-year, or seasonal preferences do not constitute a committed deadline under this factor.
 Construction-complete date. The calendar date on which the customer's construction of the site
was certified complete and ready for utility energization steps. Where more than one date is recorded,
the earlier of (a) the customer's written notice of construction completion and (b) the utility's on-site
verification, controls.
 Queue date as tiebreaker. The interconnection queue date of the site's underlying application, used
only to break a tie among sites that rank equally on factors (1), (2), and (3).
External advocacy, correspondence volume, elected-official inquiries, and stakeholder communications
received in relation to a site do not enter the ranking. Ranking is determined from the raw attributes above,
evidenced by the source documents in §3.
§3  DOCUMENTATION
For each deployment window the DER Program Office shall assemble a deployment worksheet listing
every site meeting the eligibility conditions of §1, with the following fields drawn from the identified system

 Site name and interconnection application ID (DER Program queue).
 Customer / party of record and site service address (DER Program queue).
 Nameplate capacity and program-scope classification per DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 (application file).

(Standards Engineering).
 Construction-complete date and source of certification (project construction file).
 Contracted in-service or grant-funding deadline, if any, with the executed instrument establishing it
attached by reference (customer submission).
 Essential-service classification, if any, with the customer's facility classification of record attached by
reference (application file).
 Interconnection queue date (DER Program queue).
The worksheet shall record the §2 factor on which each ranked site qualifies. Sites that do not qualify at
ranks (1) or (2) are ranked by (3) with (4) as tiebreaker. The worksheet, the ranked deployment list, and
the assigned equipment-set identifiers shall be retained in the DER Program equipment-planning file for
the applicable window and provided to the SOC concurrent with the coordination step described in §5.

Amendments to the worksheet arising after issuance — for example, receipt of previously missing
documentation for a listed site, or arrival of a new site into the waiting population — shall be recorded in an
addendum bearing its own date; prior ranked lists are not overwritten.
§4  VENDOR ENGAGEMENT EXPECTATIONS

data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":61,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{"success":true,"page":{"id":42,"path":"der-program/standards/dps-07-rev2-distribution-protection-standard","title":"DPS-07 Rev2 Distribution Protection Standard","description":"Distribution Protection Standard Rev 2 effective 09/15/2023 with POI recloser requirements","content":"# DPS-07 Rev2 Distribution Protection Standard\n\nDPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023\nPage 1\nALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING\nDISTRIBUTION PROTECTION STANDARD\nDoc no.\nRev\nDate\nOwner\nDPS-07\nRev 2\n09/15/2023\nAlleniom Standards Engineering\nEffective date: 09/15/2023\nSupersedes: DPS-07 Rev 1 (11/04/2019)\nClassification: Engineering Standard — Distribution Protection\nApproved by: Manager, Standards Engineering\n1. PURPOSE\nDPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources\n(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault\nclearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the\nutility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to\nthe distribution network.\nThis standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective\ndevices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards\nEngineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope\nprojects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.\n2. SCOPE\nThis standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service\nterritory, including but not limited to:\n1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).\n2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).\n3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to\nthe distribution system through the point of common coupling.\nSub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this\nstandard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall\napply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.\nNon-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any\noperating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection\nguidance.\n3. REFERENCES\nThe following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:\n IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with\nAssociated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.\n IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.\n IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible\nAutomatic Circuit Reclosers.\n ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.\n\n\n---\n\nDPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023 Page 2\n Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.\n Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.\n4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS\n4.1 General\nEvery distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment\nsufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:\n(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility\nreclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.\n(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on\nthe utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection\nstandard.\n(c)Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption\nbetween the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.\n(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is\ncleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary\ntripping of either.\n4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement\nEvery export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection\n(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.\nThe POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:\n1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,\ncurrent and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and\noperated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary\nconductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications\nbackhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.\n2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit\ninterrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per\nDistribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.\n3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,\nwith settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:\n— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),\n— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,\n— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,\n— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,\n— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power\nbackstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,\n— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.\n4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the\ncontrol cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of\ncommunications shall not defeat local protection.\nWhere a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering\ndetermination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.\n\n---\n\nDPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023\nPage 3\n5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect\noperable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of\nclearance holds.\n6. Location. 1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
 IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
 IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
 IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
 ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.

4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c)Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.

POL-QM-05  ·  Rev 3  ·  Date 03/15/2025  ·  Owner: DER Program Office\nQueue Management & Withdrawal Policy\nApplies to:  All DER Interconnection Program applications (≥500 kW) administered by the DER Program Office.\nSupersedes:  POL-QM-05 Rev 2 (07/12/2023).\nOwner:  DER Program Office.\nApproving Authority:  Manager, Interconnection Studies.\n§1  Purpose\nThis policy sets out the internal procedures by which the DER Program Office administers queue integrity and orderly withdrawal of applications from the active DER interconnection queue. It is intended to ensure that:\n(a)\tapplications are closed only on a documented basis;\n(b)\tqueue positions are established, retained, and released in a manner consistent with the Company's APUC-filed interconnection tariff (in particular §12.3, §12.4, and §12.6) and with the DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01);\n(c)\tstaff processing intake, screening, and case-management actions apply a single, uniform standard when an application appears stalled, abandoned, superseded, or replaced by a subsequent filing at the same site; and\n(d)\tthe record supporting each queue action is complete and auditable.\nNothing in this policy modifies the tariff. Where any provision of this policy is read to conflict with the tariff or with an applicable engineering standard, the tariff and the standard control, and the conflict shall be referred to Regulatory Affairs for reconciliation.\n§2  Withdrawal upon Customer Request\nA stalled or abandoned application is closed only upon receipt of the customer's official withdrawal confirmation, provided in writing by letter or email. Where a new filing is submitted for the same site while a prior application remains open, the program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing; the new application takes its own queue date at time of filing. No queue-date inheritance is permitted.\n§2.1  Scope of §2\nThis §2 governs closure of applications that have not been the subject of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under tariff §12.4. It applies where:\n(a)\tthe customer has ceased substantive engagement with the program (whether by prolonged non-response, express indication of intent not to proceed, or otherwise);\n(b)\tthe customer or an authorized developer has requested closure of an application without such a notice having issued; or\n(c)\ta new application is filed for the same site (as identified by service address, meter, or point of common coupling) while a prior application for that site remains in the active queue.\n§2.2  Form of the Withdrawal Confirmation\nTo constitute an “official withdrawal confirmation” for purposes of this §2, the writing must:\n(a)\tbe from the applicant of record (or from a person whose authority to act for the applicant has been established on the record — e.g., the developer named as the applicant's designated representative on the intake form);\n(b)\tbe received by the DER Program Office by letter or email, addressed to der.program@alleniom.com or delivered to the DER Program Office at the letterhead address above;\n(c)\tidentify the application by application identifier (PXA-YYYY-NNNN) and site; and\n(d)\tstate expressly that the applicant withdraws the identified application.\nNeither an oral communication (telephone, meeting, or voicemail), nor a status note recorded by staff, nor the mere filing of a new application at the same site, shall by itself constitute the official withdrawal confirmation required under this §2.\n§2.3  Procedure — Stalled or Abandoned Application (Non-Notice Path)\nWhere staff identify an application within the scope of §2.1(a) or §2.1(b), the case handler shall:\n1.\tConfirm the application's status in the active queue and document the basis for concluding that the application is stalled or abandoned;\n2.\tPrepare and send a written communication (letter or email) to the applicant of record requesting the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation in the form specified in §2.2;\n3.\tLog the request in the case file and in the queue-management system;\n4.\tOn receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, close the application and record the closure date, the closure basis (“§2 — customer request”), and the reference to the writing on file; and\n5.\tPreserve the withdrawal writing in the case file in accordance with §4.\nAbsent receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, the application shall not be closed under this §2. If the applicant does not provide the confirmation and non-response persists, the case handler may refer the matter for issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §3.\n§2.4  Duplicate Filings at the Same Site\nWhere a new application is filed for the same site while a prior application for that site remains open in the queue:\n(a)\tThe DER Program Office shall accept the new application in the ordinary course and shall assign the new application its own queue date determined as of the date the new application is determined to be complete. The two applications shall not be merged, consolidated, or treated as continuations of a single filing.\n(d)\tWhere the applicant states a preference or expectation that the earlier queue date apply to the new filing, staff shall respond in writing that the new application's queue date is fixed by §12.3 of the tariff and by this §2.4, and that closure of the prior application does not alter the queue date of the new application.\n§2.5  Consistency with DIS-01 §7 and Tariff §12.6\nNothing in this §2 authorizes the use of a customer-requested withdrawal to reopen or amend an executed Interconnection Service Agreement. Post-execution changes to material terms of an ISA — including nameplate capacity and point of interconnection — require withdrawal-and-reapplication in accordance with DIS-01 §7 and tariff §12.6. A customer-requested withdrawal in that context establishes a new queue date for the successor application; no queue-date inheritance is permitted.\n§3  Deemed Withdrawal (Procedural Restatement of Tariff §12.4)\nFollowing issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation, if the applicant fails to respond within 30 business days, the application is deemed withdrawn.\n§3.1  Relationship to the Tariff\nThis §3 is a procedural restatement, for internal use, of the deemed-withdrawal mechanism established by tariff §12.4. In the event of any inconsistency between this §3 and §12.4, the tariff controls. Staff shall consult §12.4 for the authoritative statement of the mechanism.\n§3.2  Prerequisites to Issuance of a Notice\nThe DER Program Office shall not issue a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation unless:\n(a)\tthe application has been open in the queue and staff have been unable to advance it because of the applicant's non-response or failure to supply required information or documentation;\n(b)\tat least one prior written follow-up has been sent to the applicant identifying the item or items required and requesting response by a stated date; and\n(c)\tthe case handler has confirmed that the matter does not fall within the construction-payment default procedure under tariff §12.5, which is a distinct mechanism (project on hold, not withdrawn, while a 30-business-day payment deadline runs).\n§3.3  Form and Service of the Notice\nEvery Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall:\n(a)\tbe issued in writing on Alleniom Utilities letterhead;\n(b)\tbe served by certified mail or by verified electronic delivery, in accordance with tariff §12.4;\n(c)\tidentify the application by identifier and site;\n(d)\tstate the item(s) requiring response;\n(e)\tstate the date of issuance and the date on which the 30 business-day response window expires, computed under §3.4; If the response is non-substantive or does not cure the identified matter, the case handler shall so document and, if warranted, issue a further follow-up or a subsequent Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation.\n§3.7  Non-Substitution\nIssuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation is not a substitute for the customer-request path under §2, and the customer-request path under §2 is not a substitute for the deemed-withdrawal path under §3. The log shall include, at minimum: application identifier; site; date of issuance; method of service; response deadline (computed under §3.4); response received (date and disposition, if any); and closure date (if any). The log is subject to periodic reconciliation against the on-hold queue report; unreconciled entries shall be brought to the attention of the Manager, Interconnection Studies.\n§4.4  Retention\nCase files and log entries shall be retained in accordance with the Company's records retention schedule for regulated interconnection records. Rev Date Owner\nTCS-02 Rev 1 06/01/2021 Alleniom Standards Engineering\nDocument title: Telemetry & Communications Standard\nApplies to: Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities interconnected to the Alleniom Utilities\ndistribution system within the DER Program scope\nEffective date: 06/01/2021\nApproving authority: Manager, Standards Engineering\n§1   PURPOSE\nThis standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time\ntelemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities\nand the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data\ncontent, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a\nDER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data\nAcquisition (SCADA) system.\nTCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited\nto telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective\nfunctions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the\nstandards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the\nscope of this document.\n§2   SCOPE\nTCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose\nnameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER\nhandled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.\nTCS-02 applies to:\n a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).\n b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).\n c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the\naggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.\n d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER\ncommissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or\ncapacity change requiring a new interconnection application.\n4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 2Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02\nWhere a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common\ncoupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the\naggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.\n§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS\n§3.1   Ownership and installation\nEach in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)\ninstalled at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,\nowned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.\nThe customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC\nservice, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU\ninstallation drawing.\n§3.3   Functional requirements\nEach RTU shall, at minimum:\n a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station\ninstrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.\n b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end\nprocessors over an approved communications path (§4).\n c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum\nof seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon\nrestoration.\n d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as\ndiagnostic points.\n e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom\nSCADA/EMS Engineering only.\n§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements\nThe RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation\ndrawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a\ndedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour\noutage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.\n§3.5   Time synchronization\nThe RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)\ntime or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a\ntimestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.\n§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification\n§3.2   Approved models\nThe utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU\nservice: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power\nplant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the\nutility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 3\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\nPrior to the RTU being accepted as commissioned, Alleniom shall perform an end-to-end\npoint-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,\nexercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.\nCommissioning of the RTU is a prerequisite to the telemetry condition stated in §5.\n§4   COMMUNICATIONS\n§4.1   Communications transport\nThe RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by\nSCADA/EMS Engineering:\n a.   Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or\n b.   Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or\n c.   Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held\nby Alleniom.\nCustomer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.\nWhere site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for\ninterconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.\n§4.2   SCADA protocol\nThe RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure\nAuthentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration\nparameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —\nshall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.\n§4.3   Availability\nThe end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a\nmonthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent\nloss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be\ncorrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected\nequipment.\n§4.4   Address and IP management\nAll IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and\nAlleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate\nconnections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration\nrecord.\n§5   TELEMETRY CONDITION FOR PERMISSION TO OPERATE\n§5.   ≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry.\nThis requirement applies to all in-scope DER sites, including aggregated facilities under\nDIS-01 §3.4.\nLive telemetry, for the purposes of §5, means that the RTU installed under §3 is:\n a.   Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;\n\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 4\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\n b.   Communicating with Alleniom SCADA over an approved transport (§4) at the refresh\ncadence required by §6; and\n c.   Presenting all required data points (§6) as valid (not stale, not forced, not flagged\nbad-quality) at the SCADA operator display at the moment Permission to Operate (PTO) is\nissued.\nCompliance with §5 is confirmed by the SOC Shift Supervisor on shift at the time PTO is\nrequested. The SOC's confirmation is recorded against the interconnection file. PTO shall not be\nissued to any in-scope DER site until §5 is satisfied.\n§6   DATA POINTS AND REFRESH RATES\n§6.1   Required data points\nEach in-scope DER site shall present, at minimum, the following analog and status points to\nAlleniom SCADA. Where the site's arrangement includes multiple inverter blocks or multiple\naggregated facilities behind a common POI, values shall be reported both individually per block\nand as a facility total.\nAnalog values (per site, and per block where applicable):\nPoint\nUnits\nSign convention\nReal power, net export at POI\nkW\nExport positive\nReactive power, net at POI\nkVAr\nAbsorbing positive\nPOI voltage, per phase\nV\n—\nPOI current, per phase\nA\n—\nFrequency at POI\nHz\n—\nGross generation (per inverter block)\nkW\nGeneration positive\nAuxiliary/parasitic load (where separately metered)\nkW\nLoad positive\nCumulative energy delivered\nkWh\nExport positive\nCumulative energy received\nkWh\nImport positive\nAmbient / cabinet temperature (RTU health)\n°C\n—\nStatus and diagnostic points:\nPoint\nDescription\nSite online / offline\nAggregate operating state of the DER\nInverter/PCS block status\nPer block: run, standby, fault\nCommunications heartbeat\nRTU-to-SCADA path health\nTime-sync quality\nGNSS/NTP discipline status\nConfiguration version\nActive RTU configuration identifier\nAlarm summary\nRolled-up device alarm state\n§6.2   Refresh rates\n\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 5\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\nAnalog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3\nClass 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than\nevery sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an\nintegrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be\nreported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.\n§6.3   Data quality\nEvery value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,\nrestart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the\nRTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be\nreported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.\n§6.4   Retention\nAlleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six\n(36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,\nengineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.\n§7   CYBERSECURITY\n§7.1   Applicability\nThe RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any\ncustomer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this\nsection. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security\nprogram consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.\n§7.2   Access control\nLocal and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to\nAlleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication\nagainst Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are\nmanaged by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.\n§7.3   Communications security\nDNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All\ncommunications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an\nAlleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates\nshall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.\n§7.4   Firmware, configuration, and change management\nRTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following\nthe Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a\ncryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or\nreconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.\n§7.5   Logging and monitoring\nThe RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,\nand firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.\nAnomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response\nprocedure.\n\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 6\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\n§7.6   Physical security\nThe RTU shall be housed in a locked, tamper-evident enclosure. Enclosure keys, cores, and any\nphysical access tokens are held by Alleniom. Physical intrusion of the enclosure shall generate a\nstatus point (tamper alarm) reported to SCADA under §6.\n§7.7   Incident response\nThe customer shall report, without delay, any known or suspected compromise of the RTU, its\nenclosure, its communications transport, or any interface between customer equipment and\nutility-owned telemetry equipment. Reports shall be directed to the Alleniom SOC and to\nSCADA/EMS Engineering.\n§7.8   Decommissioning\nAt end of life, the RTU and its cryptographic material are returned to Alleniom for secure disposal.\nCustomer equipment previously interfaced to the RTU shall be sanitized of any Alleniom-provided\ncredentials before it is repurposed or disposed of.\nEnd of TCS-02.","content_type":"markdown","editor":"markdown","is_published":true,"is_private":false,"locale":"en","created_at":"2026-11-27T02:27:42.791943+00:00","updated_at":"2026-11-27T02:27:42.791943+00:00","tags":["standards","telemetry"],"author_name":"Evan Solberg","author_email":"evan.solberg@alleniom.com"},"error":""}"}],"structuredContent":{"success":true,"page":{"id":48,"path":"der-program/standards/tcs-02-telemetry-comms-standard","title":"TCS-02 Telemetry Comms Standard","description":"Telemetry and Communications Standard effective 06/01/2021 requiring RTU and SCADA for sites 500 kW and above","content":"# TCS-02 Telemetry Comms Standard

Acquisition (SCADA) system.

to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
scope of this document.

nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.

 a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).

 d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.

§12.2 Scope of the DER Interconnection Program
The DER Interconnection Program administered under this section applies to applications for DER
interconnection at or above five hundred kilowatts (≥500 kW). Within the Program, DER shall be
classified according to the DER Interconnection Standard as follows:
(a)  Commercial small-scale DER — five hundred kilowatts to one megawatt (500 kW – 1
MW);
(b)  Medium-scale DER — one megawatt to five megawatts (1 MW – 5 MW).
The Program scope threshold is ≥500 kW. DER below five hundred kilowatts (sub-500 kW),
whether commercial or residential, are not administered under this section and shall instead be
processed under the Company's Simplified Small-Systems Process, which is filed separately
and is outside the DER Interconnection Program.
Aggregation, controlled-capacity recognition, and shared point-of-interconnection eligibility are
addressed in the DER Interconnection Standard and shall control the classification of any facility
whose nameplate rating, aggregate site rating, or point of common coupling brings it within

§12.3 Application Intake and Queue Position
A complete application shall establish the applicant's queue position as of the date the Company
determines the application to be complete. Applications determined to be incomplete shall be
returned with a written deficiency notice identifying each item requiring cure and the date by which
cure is required. Queue position is not transferable between applications except as expressly
provided in the DER Interconnection Standard.
§12.4 Deemed Withdrawal Following Notice of Impending Withdrawal or Cancellation
Upon issuance of a formal written Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation by the
Company, the applicant shall have thirty (30) business days from the date of the notice to submit
a substantive response curing the matter identified therein. If the applicant fails to respond within
thirty (30) business days, the application shall be deemed withdrawn and shall be closed from the
active queue without further action of the Company.
For purposes of this section, “business days” shall exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and federal
legal public holidays observed within the response window. Without limitation, the following
federal holidays falling within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized
as non-business days and shall not be counted:
Holiday
Observed Date
Memorial Day
05/26/2025
Juneteenth National Independence Day
06/19/2025
Independence Day
07/04/2025
The Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall be served in writing (certified mail or
verified electronic delivery) and shall state the date of issuance, the response deadline computed
under this section, and the consequence of non-response. The Company shall maintain a log of all
notices issued, dates of service, and dispositions.

§12.5 Construction-Payment Defaults
Where a construction work order or interconnection facilities invoice becomes payable and the
customer has not remitted the amount due, the Company shall inform the customer in writing of
the outstanding balance and shall issue a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days from
the date of that written notice.
For so long as the thirty (30) business-day payment deadline is running, the affected project shall
remain on hold in the queue and shall NOT be deemed withdrawn. The construction-payment
default procedure under this §12.5 is distinct from, and shall not be conflated with, the
deemed-withdrawal procedure under §12.4; the two mechanisms have different triggers, different
consequences, and different cure paths.
Upon receipt of full payment prior to expiration of the deadline, the Company shall promptly
release the hold and resume the affected work in queue order. If the deadline expires without
payment, the Company may pursue such remedies as are available under the applicable
Interconnection Service Agreement and this tariff, including, as a separate and subsequent step,
issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §12.4.

§12.6 Interconnection Service Agreement
Interconnection service shall commence only upon execution of an Interconnection Service
Agreement (“ISA”) and the Company's written Permission to Operate. Material terms of an
executed ISA, including but not limited to nameplate facility capacity and the designated point of
interconnection, may not be modified by amendment. Post-execution changes to such material
terms require withdrawal of the affected application and re-application in accordance with the DER
Interconnection Standard.
§12.7 Nondiscriminatory Queue-Order Processing of Applications
Applications shall be processed by the Company in queue order on a nondiscriminatory basis.
No applicant shall be advanced or disadvantaged in the processing sequence by reason of
identity, affiliation, customer class, geography, or any other factor not expressly provided for in this
tariff or in the DER Interconnection Standard.
Scope note. This §12.7 applies to APPLICATION PROCESSING only — that is, to the
sequencing of screening, technical review, study assignment, and issuance of interconnection
determinations. Utility construction sequencing and the scheduling and allocation of constrained
utility-owned equipment (including, without limitation, remote terminal units,
point-of-interconnection reclosers, and other supply-limited devices) are not governed by this
section. Such matters are addressed under the Company's operating guidelines, including OG-17
(Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline), which sets forth the criticality factors and
prioritization criteria applicable to constrained equipment. Nothing in this §12.7 shall be construed
to require the Company to sequence construction or equipment deployment in queue order where
OG-17 or another operating guideline provides a different criticality-based ordering.

**From:** Rosa Camarena <rosa.camarena@brookfenusd.org>
**To:** der.program@alleniom.com
**Date:** Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:42:18 -0500
**Subject:** Urgent: school array energization priority
**Cc:** Dana Whitcomb <dana.whitcomb@alleniom.com>, Harriet Ngoyi <harriet.ngoyi@alleniom.com>

---

To the DER Program Office:

I am writing again — and I want to be direct about the fact that this is not the first, second, or third time I have raised this with your office — to ask for a firm answer on when Alleniom Utilities intends to energize the two solar arrays serving Brookfen Unified School District. This message is dated 06/30/2025 and I would like a written response before the end of next week.

The two arrays in question, and their status on our side, are as follows:

  • Brookfen North High School Array — 720 kW. Construction was declared complete by our contractor on 04/18/2025. The local electrical inspector closed out the installation the same week. The system has been standing idle, energized-ready, for more than ten weeks.

  • Brookfen West Elementary Array — 640 kW. Construction was declared complete on 05/23/2025. Inspection was closed out shortly thereafter. This system has now been standing idle for over a month.

Neither array has been energized. Neither array has a firm energization date on record with the District. Each time our office contacts your program inbox we are told that a component — variously described as a "telemetry unit" or an "RTU" — has not yet been delivered by your supplier, and that we are somewhere in a queue behind other sites. What we have never been given, in writing, is the position of our sites in that queue, the identity of the sites ahead of us, or the basis on which those sites are being served ahead of ours.

I have to tell you plainly that the patience of the Brookfen school board and the District's superintendent is exhausted. The 2025–2026 school year begins for our students on 08/26/2025. Both of these arrays were financed, in significant part, on the strength of first-year operating-cost savings that were built into the District's adopted budget for that same school year and presented to our board and to the community at public meetings. Every additional week that these systems sit dark is a week of budgeted savings the District will not realize and will have to explain to the board, to our parents, and to the taxpayers of Brookfen who approved the underlying bond measure. Our high school's building-systems curriculum was also structured around students being able to observe the array in operation from the beginning of the term; that piece of the school year is now at risk of slipping into the second semester or being cut altogether.

You will by now have received the Alleron Municipal League's letter of 06/20/2025, signed by Executive Director Alden Pryce, escalating this same set of concerns on behalf of the District and thirteen other League members. Brookfen USD is one of the members named in that letter and stands fully behind the requests it contains. This message is not a substitute for the League's letter; it is intended to make the District's individual position, and the specifics of our two sites, unmistakable to your office.

What I am asking for, directly, is this: in the next allocation of the equipment your program office is holding up as the constraint — the RTU / telemetry units your staff have referenced in prior calls — I am asking Alleniom Utilities to advance the District's two waiting arrays ahead of the other sites presently competing for those units. Brookfen North completed construction on 04/18/2025 and Brookfen West on 05/23/2025. Both are public school facilities. Both have children returning to the building in eight weeks. Neither array can wait for a second or third delivery cycle without meaningful harm to the District's fiscal position and to the educational program these systems were installed to support.

If there is a formal process for requesting that our two sites be advanced in your next equipment allocation, please tell me what that process is and I will follow it today. If there is not, please treat this message as our written request under whatever mechanism your program uses to weigh these decisions, and please confirm receipt.

I am copying Ms. Whitcomb and Ms. Ngoyi so that this request is on the record with senior distribution operations and regulatory affairs, and so that no one at your program office is later in a position to say the District did not put this in writing in time.

I would like a written reply — not a call-back, a written reply — by close of business Friday, 07/11/2025. Silence past that date will require the District to raise this matter again through the League and, if necessary, directly with the Commission's Energy Resources Division, whose staff we understand is already tracking this program.

I am available at (612) 448-0311 during District business hours if it would help to talk any of this through. I would strongly prefer to resolve it with your office.

Regards,

Rosa Camarena
Facilities Director
Brookfen Unified School District
1725 Grantway Drive, Brookfen, Alleron 12BR
(612) 448-0311

Established referral form and per-site engineering determination path.\nRev 2\n03/24/2025\nReissued in conjunction with Bulletin EB-2025-03. §3 rewritten to state routing rule\nfor standards conflicts; Form ER-11 fields expanded to capture site type and feeder;\nprecedent register appended.\n§1 PURPOSE\nERP-9 establishes the procedure by which an interconnection application encountering a standards\nconflict, a silence between standards, or site conditions falling outside the assumptions of a tabulated\nrequirement is referred to a per-site protection/SCADA engineering determination. The procedure exists so\nthat documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against\nactive applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,\non a schedule stated in §4.\nThis procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER\nProgram. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection\nStandard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.\n\n\n---\n\n§2 SCOPE\nERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one\nor more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system\nimpact study:\n(1)  Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to\nthe affected site.\n(2)  An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic\non which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an\nexception).\n(3)  The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in\nlight of the site's specific protection arrangement.\nSub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application\nof ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration\nwarrants site-specific protection engineering input.\nNothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a\ndetermination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).\n§3 REFERRAL ROUTING\nAny standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site\nprotection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;\neach site is resolved on its own protection scheme.\nThe reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11\n(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection\ndiagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's\nprotection arrangement. The affected application\nremains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the\nreferred question shall proceed in parallel.\nThe per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection\nEngineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution\nProtection Engineering, and is filed with the application record.
