§1 PURPOSE
ERP-9 establishes the procedure by which an interconnection application encountering a standards
conflict, a silence between standards, or site conditions falling outside the assumptions of a tabulated
requirement is referred to a per-site protection/SCADA engineering determination. The procedure exists so
that documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against
active applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,
on a schedule stated in §4.
This procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER
Program. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection
Standard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.


---

§2 SCOPE
ERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one
or more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system
impact study:
(1)  Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to
the affected site.
(2)  An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic
on which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an
exception).
(3)  The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in
light of the site's specific protection arrangement.
Sub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application
of ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration
warrants site-specific protection engineering input.
Nothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a
determination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).
§3 REFERRAL ROUTING
Any standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site
protection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;
each site is resolved on its own protection scheme.
The reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11
(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection
diagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's
protection arrangement. Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11 to Distribution
Protection Engineering; where SCADA/EMS input is required, the Manager, Distribution Protection
Engineering routes a copy to the SCADA/EMS Engineering group for concurrent review.
Referral does not itself alter the application's status in the DER Program queue. The affected application
remains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the
referred question shall proceed in parallel.
The per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection
Engineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and is filed with the application record. The determination is binding for the
referred site and does not create a general rule across the program; a subsequent site presenting a similar
question is referred and determined on its own facts.

INTERCONNECTION SERVICE AGREEMENT
Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
Doc no. ISA-Harkwell-Ridge · Rev Final · Date 07/03/2025 · Owner: DER Program Office — Contracts
Agreement No.: ISA-Harkwell-Ridge
Project: Harkwell Ridge Solar
Application No.: PXA-2024-0117
This Interconnection Service Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into by and between Alleniom Utilities, an investor-owned electric utility organized under the laws of the State of Alleron, with principal offices at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA (EIN 36-4820917) (the “Company”), and Hailbouy Solar, with offices at 2200 Ridge Point Road, Suite 400, Halston, Alleron 03HA (the “Interconnection Customer”), each a “Party” and collectively the “Parties.” This Agreement is effective as of the date last executed below.
RECITALS
WHEREAS, the Interconnection Customer filed with the Company an application for interconnection service, designated PXA-2024-0117, on 06/17/2024, in respect of a 2.2 MW single-axis-tracker ground-mount photovoltaic generating facility known as Harkwell Ridge Solar (the “Facility”), to be interconnected to the Company's distribution system at a point on Feeder ALN-042;
WHEREAS, the Company completed technical screening, system impact and facilities studies for the Facility in accordance with the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4, and issued a final study determination approving the Facility for execution of an Interconnection Service Agreement at the capacity and point of interconnection described in the application as filed;
WHEREAS, the Company's tariff, as filed with and approved by the Alleron Public Utilities Commission, governs the interconnection of distributed energy resources of the Facility's class and forms an integral part of the terms and conditions of interconnection service provided hereunder;
WHEREAS, the Parties intend by this Agreement to establish the terms, conditions, rights and obligations under which the Facility will be permitted to parallel with, and export energy to, the Company's distribution system;
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and undertakings set forth herein, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS
1.1 Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Company's filed tariff (the “Tariff”) and in the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4 (the “DIS”).
1.2 For the purposes of this Agreement, and without limitation of the foregoing:
“Facility” means the generating equipment, ancillary equipment, and all interconnection facilities described in Article 2 hereof.
“Point of Interconnection” or “POI” means the physical point at which the Facility is electrically connected to the Company's distribution system, as identified in Article 2.
“Standards” means the standards and specifications identified in Article 4, each as in effect on the Effective Date and as such may be amended, superseded, or reissued by the Company in accordance with its ordinary regulatory practice.
“Effective Date” has the meaning given in Article 3.
“Certified Equipment List” or “CEL” means the Company's then-current Certified Equipment List published by Standards Engineering.
ARTICLE 2 — DESCRIPTION OF FACILITY
2.1 Project designation. Harkwell Ridge Solar (Application PXA-2024-0117).
2.2 Interconnection Customer. Hailbouy Solar.
2.3 Facility technology. Photovoltaic generation, single-axis-tracker ground-mount configuration.
2.4 Nameplate export capacity. 2.2 MW (AC) at the Point of Interconnection.
2.5 Point of Interconnection (POI). A three-phase primary tap on Feeder ALN-042, at the pole FKDN54D.
2.6 Point of Common Coupling (PCC). Coincident with the Point of Interconnection identified in Section 2.5.
2.7 Material terms. The capacity, technology, and Point of Interconnection stated in this Article are material terms of this Agreement.
ARTICLE 3 — TERM AND EFFECTIVE DATE
3.1 Effective Date. This Agreement is effective as of 07/03/2025 (the “Effective Date”), being the date on which the last of the two Parties has executed this Agreement.
3.2 Term. This Agreement shall remain in full force and effect from the Effective Date until terminated in accordance with its terms or superseded by a successor agreement between the Parties.
3.3 Continuing obligations. The obligations of the Parties in respect of indemnity, limitation of liability, confidentiality, and dispute resolution shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement.
ARTICLE 4 — INTERCONNECTION STANDARDS
4.1 Governing standards. The Facility shall at all times be designed, constructed, commissioned, operated, and maintained in conformity with the following Company standards and any successor or superseding editions thereof:
(a) DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard (effective 03/01/2024);
(b) DPS-07 Rev 2 — Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023);
(c) TCS-02 — Telemetry and Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021); and
(d) CEL-2025-Q2 — Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025), as such may be superseded from time to time.
4.2 Order of precedence. In the event of any inconsistency among the documents constituting this Agreement, the following order of precedence shall govern: (i) the Tariff; (ii) the applicable Company Standards enumerated in Section 4.1; (iii) the body of this Agreement.
4.3 Compliance with successor standards. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to relieve the Interconnection Customer from the obligation to conform the Facility to successor or superseding editions of the Standards as and when they take effect, in accordance with the transition provisions of the applicable Standard.
ARTICLE 5 — METERING AND TELEMETRY
5.1 Metering. Revenue-quality metering shall be provided at the Point of Interconnection in accordance with the Tariff and the Company's metering specifications. Meters shall be owned, installed, tested, and maintained by the Company at the Interconnection Customer's cost, and shall be sealed at all times.
5.2 Telemetry. In accordance with TCS-02 §5, the Interconnection Customer shall install, at its cost, provisions for a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) and shall make available all analog and binary status DNP3 points required by the Company's Telemetry and Communications Standard, together with such communication paths and standing-power provisions as the Company requires for SCADA integration.
5.3 Commissioning of monitoring and control. Satisfactory commissioning and continuous availability of the telemetry described in Section 5.2 are conditions precedent to Permission to Operate. The Facility shall not be paralleled with the Company's distribution system in the absence of live utility telemetry, and any loss of telemetry after Permission to Operate shall be reported and remediated as provided in TCS-02.
5.4 Data and access rights. The Interconnection Customer grants the Company such rights of access to the Facility, and such rights to receive and use metering and telemetry data, as are necessary for the Company to discharge its obligations under the Tariff and applicable Standards.
ARTICLE 6 — PAYMENT TERMS
6.1 Construction work order. The Interconnection Customer shall pay the Company for the construction of upgrades and interconnection facilities in accordance with the construction work order issued under this Agreement, on the schedule and in the amounts set forth therein, and in accordance with Tariff §12.5.
6.2 Invoicing. Invoices shall be issued by the Company and shall be due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the invoice date, unless otherwise expressly provided in the construction work order. Amounts not paid when due shall bear interest at the rate set forth in the Tariff.
6.3 Payment default. In the event of non-payment, the Company shall provide the Interconnection Customer written notice and a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days in accordance with Tariff §12.5. Business days exclude weekends and federal holidays. During the pendency of any such deadline the Facility shall remain subject to any construction or commissioning hold ordered by the Company.
6.4 Ongoing operational charges. All charges, credits, and settlements applicable to interconnection service and associated ancillary services shall be as set forth in the Tariff.

Alleniom Utilities — Regulatory Affairs
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
TO: DER Program Manager
CC: Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations
Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
FROM: Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
DATE: 07/01/2025
SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking
1. Confirmation of directive
This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
4. Reporting cadence
The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.
Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
5. General provisions
Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action.

ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1. The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2. Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3. Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4. Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.

§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.
Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.
§4.3  Documentation.
The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
include, at minimum:

the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;

for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
by the Standards Engineer of record;

§1 Purpose and Scope
This standard establishes the technical and procedural requirements for interconnection of distributed energy
resources (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. It is based on IEEE 1547-2018 and applicable state
interconnection rules filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC), and it applies to all DER classes
defined in §3.
DIS-01 Rev 4 governs:
• classification of DER facilities by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling (§3);
• eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);
• recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);
• protective and control equipment requirements by class and category (§5);

DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard

Page 1

• treatment of post-execution changes to executed interconnection service agreements (§7).
This standard is read together with the APUC-filed interconnection tariff (§12). Where a topic is addressed by both
this standard and the tariff, the tariff controls. Requirements for real-time monitoring and communications integration
are established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.

§2 References
The following documents are referenced within this standard. Unless otherwise noted, the latest published revision
applies.
• IEEE 1547-2018 — IEEE Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources
with Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
• DPS-07 Rev 2 — Alleniom Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023). Establishes distribution
protection requirements including protective devices at points of interconnection with export-capable in-scope
facilities.
• TCS-02 — Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021). Governs utility-owned RTU
installation and SCADA telemetry for DER at and above the program-scope threshold; establishes the condition
for permission to operate.
• CEL-2025-Q2 — Alleniom Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025). Listing basis: UL 1741-SB and UL
3141. The CEL front matter restates §3.6 of this standard.
• ERP-9 — Alleniom Engineering Referral Procedure (Form ER-11). §3 routes any standards

Definitions of terms used in this standard follow IEEE 1547-2018 and, where applicable, the definitions in the
APUC-filed tariff. The terms aggregate nameplate capacity and point of common coupling (PCC) have the meanings
assigned by IEEE 1547-2018 and reflected in Company practice. The terms point of interconnection (POI),
export-capable, and pure-generation site are used in accordance with their ordinary meaning in utility
interconnection practice.

§3 DER Classification
DER facilities are classified by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling, in accordance with
IEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.
Commercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW; medium-scale 1 MW–5 MW; program scope ≥500 kW; sub-500 kW DER
(commercial and residential) is handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process, outside the DER Program.

The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.

§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.

§3.2 Point of common coupling
The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.

§3.3 Determination on the basis of application
Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
the address of record govern.

§3.4 Aggregation
Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.
Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
resulting program-scope determination.
An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
the Company existing-DER register.

§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.

DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard

Page 3

 DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024

The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:
1. Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
2. Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.

§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.
Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:
1. A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
setpoint range.
2. An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.

§1 Purpose and Scope
This standard establishes the technical and procedural requirements for interconnection of distributed energy
resources (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. It is based on IEEE 1547-2018 and applicable state
interconnection rules filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC), and it applies to all DER classes
defined in §3.
DIS-01 Rev 4 governs:
• classification of DER facilities by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling (§3);
• eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);
• recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);
• protective and control equipment requirements by class and category (§5);

DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard

• treatment of post-execution changes to executed interconnection service agreements (§7).
This standard is read together with the APUC-filed interconnection tariff (§12). Where a topic is addressed by both
this standard and the tariff, the tariff controls. Requirements for real-time monitoring and communications integration
are established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.

§2 References
The following documents are referenced within this standard. Unless otherwise noted, the latest published revision
applies.
• IEEE 1547-2018 — IEEE Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources
with Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
• DPS-07 Rev 2 — Alleniom Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023). Establishes distribution
protection requirements including protective devices at points of interconnection with export-capable in-scope
facilities.
• TCS-02 — Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021). Governs utility-owned RTU
installation and SCADA telemetry for DER at and above the program-scope threshold; establishes the condition
for permission to operate.
• CEL-2025-Q2 — Alleniom Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025). Listing basis: UL 1741-SB and UL
3141. The CEL front matter restates §3.6 of this standard.
• ERP-9 — Alleniom Engineering Referral Procedure (Form ER-11). §3 routes any standards

Definitions of terms used in this standard follow IEEE 1547-2018 and, where applicable, the definitions in the
APUC-filed tariff. The terms aggregate nameplate capacity and point of common coupling (PCC) have the meanings
assigned by IEEE 1547-2018 and reflected in Company practice. The terms point of interconnection (POI),
export-capable, and pure-generation site are used in accordance with their ordinary meaning in utility
interconnection practice.

§3 DER Classification

IEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.
Commercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW; medium-scale 1 MW–5 MW; program scope ≥500 kW; sub-500 kW DER
(commercial and residential) is handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process, outside the DER Program.

The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.

§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.

§3.2 Point of common coupling
The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.

§3.3 Determination on the basis of application
Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
the address of record govern.

§3.4 Aggregation
Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.
Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
resulting program-scope determination.
An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
the Company existing-DER register.

§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.

DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard

Page 3

 DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024

The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:
1. Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
2. Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.

§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.
Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:
1. A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
setpoint range.
2. An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.
Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:
• Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
• POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
additional utility hardware.
Enforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does
not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.
No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.
Certified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL
does not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific
certification and Control Narrative are always required.

DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard

§4 Screening and Study Process
Applications in DER Program scope proceed through initial technical screening under Interconnection Studies.
Facilities not passing initial screens may be evaluated under supplemental review per SRP-3 or advance to a system
impact study. This standard does not restate SRP-3; the daytime minimum-load convention and other screen
methodologies are prescribed there.

for the telemetry rule and to Alleniom system operations for RTU installation scheduling.
Site-level control functions required by §3.6 (Power Control System recognition), by Table 5-1 (dedicated protection
relay schemes, DER breaker arrangements), and by ERP-9 site determinations, together satisfy the
control-integration expectations of this section as applied to the specific facility.

§7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions
Post-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not
permitted for capacity or POI changes.
Scope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by
both parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without
invoking this section.
Principal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection
service agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as
executed.
Required path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of
interconnection after ISA execution shall:
1. Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;
2. File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and
3. Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.
The new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested
change is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the
applicant as involving new or existing equipment.
Other post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within
the same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the
change-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.
Downstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment
reservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in
queue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application
receives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.

§8 Records and Compliance
Interconnection Studies retains the application file, executed ISA, and study record for each in-scope facility for the
retention period established by Regulatory Affairs. Standards Engineering maintains the current revision of this
standard, the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2 and subsequent editions), and the Engineering Referral
Procedure (ERP-9) register of per-site determinations.

On behalf of the Alleron Municipal League and the fourteen member communities identified below, I write to
convey our formal and collective concern regarding the continued and, in our view, unreasonable delays
affecting commercial-scale solar interconnection projects currently stalled within Alleniom Utilities’ Distributed
Energy Resource (DER) interconnection program. This letter follows repeated informal outreach by individual
member staff to your DER Program Office over the preceding several months, outreach which has not produced
the clarity or the timely progress our members need in order to close out their local capital projects.
The League is writing on behalf of 14 municipalities and school districts across the state of Alleron whose
commercial-scale solar projects — commissioned in good faith with voter-approved bond proceeds, adopted
capital budgets, energy-savings performance contracts, and in several instances state and federal grant awards
remain suspended in your interconnection queue awaiting energization. Among the affected members are:
Brookfen Unified School District
City of Elmsworth
Darnwick Community School District
Lockmere Community School District
Cravenwood Community School District
Town of Tresbay
City of Marden Falls
Town of Holcott
Additional League members with projects in the same posture have asked to be represented collectively through
this correspondence and are prepared to be identified upon request. Every one of these projects has been
reviewed and approved by the applicable local governing body, financed through public procurement, and
constructed by licensed contractors under permits issued by the relevant authority having jurisdiction.
The projects at issue are not speculative or exploratory. They range in size from approximately 500 kW to nearly
1 MW and are installed at public schools, municipal water and wastewater treatment plants, community centers,
public libraries, and other municipal facilities. In the great majority of cases construction is complete, mechanical
and electrical inspections have been closed out by local inspectors, and equipment has been standing
energized-ready — in some instances for a period now measured in months — pending only the Company’s
authorization to interconnect and place the systems into commercial operation. Each additional month of delay
defers budgeted operating savings, extends the payback horizon presented to our members’ councils and school
boards, and in the case of grant-funded projects places committed public funding at direct risk of forfeiture.
Our members are patient partners. They understand that the interconnection of distributed generation on the
Company’s distribution system requires careful technical review and, at times, coordination with equipment
procurement, feeder studies, and protection-scheme confirmation. They are willing to meet reasonable technical
requirements. What they are not able to accept — and what this League cannot accept on their behalf — is an

 extended period of silence, shifting explanations, and open-ended hold status without a clear articulation of what
is required, by whom, and by when.
Accordingly, and in a spirit of continued cooperation, the League respectfully requests the following from
Alleniom Utilities:
1. A full accounting of current queue status. For each identified League-member project, please provide the
project’s assigned application number, current queue position, and complete processing history to date.
2. Hold reasons. For every project currently in a hold, pending, or suspended posture, please identify the
specific reason for the hold, the party responsible for the next action, the information or resource required to
release the hold, and the date the hold was established.
3. Expected energization dates. For each project, please provide the Company’s current best estimate of the
date on which Permission to Operate will be issued, together with any intermediate milestone dates
(studies, equipment delivery, witness testing, or telemetry acceptance) that inform that estimate.
4. A written response. We request the Company’s response in writing, addressed to the undersigned at the
League’s Cordwyn office, within a reasonable period consistent with the urgency our members’ councils

League’s executive office, and designated representatives of the affected members, to be scheduled at the
Company’s offices in Halston or at a mutually convenient location in Cordwyn at the Company’s preference.
The League is prepared to convene our members on short notice once the Company proposes a date.
For your awareness, a copy of this letter has been provided to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC),
Energy Resources Division, for the Division’s information. The League has taken this step not as a matter of
confrontation but out of a good-faith obligation to keep the Commission’s staff apprised of a program-level
concern affecting a substantial number of Alleron public entities across multiple service territories within the
Company’s distribution footprint. It remains our strong preference to resolve this matter directly with Alleniom
Utilities.

restoring predictable, transparent processing timelines to the DER program. Our members’ communities have
invested public funds, published expected in-service dates to their constituents, and in several cases entered
into contractual arrangements predicated on interconnection occurring by dates that are now past. The credibility
of local government energy planning across Alleron is meaningfully bound up in the outcome, and we are
confident the Company understands the seriousness with which we, our elected officials, and our school boards

correspondence from the Alleron Municipal League dated 06/20/2025 (AML Ref:

and school districts a program-level concern with the current pace of commercial-scale Distributed
Energy Resource (DER) interconnection processing on the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The
League's letter identifies delays affecting projects at public schools, municipal water and wastewater
facilities, community centers, and public libraries across multiple communities within the Company's
service territory, and raises questions regarding queue status, hold posture, and expected energization
timelines that fall within the Division's continuing oversight of the Company's APUC-filed
interconnection tariff.
The Division intends to be in a position to brief the Commission on the matter at the previously
scheduled DER program briefing on 09/10/2025. In advance of that briefing, and to permit the Division
to assess the Company's DER interconnection program on the basis of the Company's own records
rather than the League's characterization, this letter requests the following information from Alleniom
Utilities.
1. Commercial DER queue accounting.
For the commercial DER interconnection program (i.e., the ≥500 kW program-scope portfolio
administered by the Company's DER Program Office; simplified small-systems process filings are
outside the scope of this request), the Company is requested to provide a complete queue accounting as
of the most recent full week preceding the response date, including at minimum the following,
presented at the individual-application level and separately summarized in totals:
a. The count and identity of all applications currently in active processing status, together with each
application's assigned application number, applicant name, site, nameplate capacity, filing date,
current processing step, and the study or decision milestone next due.

 b.

The count and identity of all applications currently on on-hold, pending-customer,
pending-standards, or suspended status, together with the specific hold reason of record for
each, the party responsible for the next action, the information or resource required to release the
hold, and the date the hold was established.

c. The count and identity of all applications for which one or more study or processing timelines
established under the Company's filed interconnection tariff, procedures, or executed study
agreements have been exceeded as of the reporting date, together with the timeline of record, the
actual elapsed time, and the current cause of the overrun.
d. The count and identity of all applications withdrawn — whether by written applicant request, by
application of the tariff's deemed-withdrawal provision, or otherwise — during the twelve
months preceding the reporting date, together with the effective date of each withdrawal and the
recorded basis for it.
e.

The count and identity of all formal Notices of Impending Withdrawal, Notices of
Cancellation, or equivalent written notices issued by the Company to applicants during the
twelve months preceding the reporting date, together with the notice date, the date sent, the
method of service, the response deadline computed under the tariff, and the current disposition
(response received / no response / deemed withdrawn / other).

Where any of the foregoing counts is materially affected by data-integrity items known to the Company
(for example, timing differences, reconciliation items, or other known data-quality issues), the Company is

requested to identify those items and provide the counts both as they presently appear in the Company's
queue records and as the Company understands the underlying facts to be.
2. Backlog-cause summary.
The Company is further requested to provide a written summary describing, in the Company's own
characterization, the principal causes of the current backlog in the commercial DER interconnection
program. The summary should address at a minimum: application volume relative to processing
capacity; the availability and lead time of utility-owned equipment required for energization (including
but not limited to RTU and protection equipment); the status of any internal standards reconciliation
activity affecting screening or protection determinations; the sufficiency of certified-equipment
references relied upon by the Company; the sufficiency of hosting-capacity information made available
to prospective applicants; and any other factors the Company identifies as materially contributing to the
current queue posture. Supporting quantitative material (equipment delivery schedules, staffing
utilization, study cycle times, and the like) is welcome and, where practicable, requested.

corresponding item. Responses should be received by the Division sufficiently in advance of the
09/10/2025 briefing to allow the Division adequate review; the Division requests that the Company
provide its response no later than 08/22/2025, and, where any portion of the response cannot be
furnished by that date, that the Company so advise the Division in writing no later than 08/08/2025 with
an explanation and a proposed alternative date.

 This request is issued in the ordinary course of the Division's monitoring of interconnection program
performance under the Company's APUC-filed tariff. The Division has no present view as to the merits
of the underlying matter and takes no position on the specific project-level concerns raised in the
League's 06/20/2025 letter, which remain properly a matter between the League's member entities and

and backlog-cause information described above, together with the Company's plan for restoring
predictable processing to the program. The Division remains available to discuss scope, format, or
timing questions at Company request.

response.

Definitions of terms used in this standard follow IEEE 1547-2018 and, where applicable, the definitions in the
APUC-filed tariff. The terms aggregate nameplate capacity and point of common coupling (PCC) have the meanings
assigned by IEEE 1547-2018 and reflected in Company practice. The terms point of interconnection (POI),
export-capable, and pure-generation site are used in accordance with their ordinary meaning in utility
interconnection practice.

§3 DER Classification
DER facilities are classified by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling, in accordance with
IEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.
Commercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW; medium-scale 1 MW–5 MW; program scope ≥500 kW; sub-500 kW DER
(commercial and residential) is handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process, outside the DER Program.

The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.

§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.

§3.2 Point of common coupling
The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.

§3.3 Determination on the basis of application
Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
the address of record govern.

§3.4 Aggregation
Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.
Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
resulting program-scope determination.
An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
the Company existing-DER register.

§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.

The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:
1. Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
2. Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.

§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.

program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:
1. A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the

§3.4 Environmental and station-service requirements
The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation

dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.
§3.5 Time synchronization
The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.

§4 COMMUNICATIONS
§4.1 Communications transport
The RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by
SCADA/EMS Engineering:
•

a. Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or

•

b. Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or

•

c. Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held
by Alleniom.

Customer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.
Where site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for
interconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.
§4.2 SCADA protocol
The RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure
Authentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration
parameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —
shall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§4.3 Availability
The end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a
monthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent
loss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be
corrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected
equipment.
§4.4 Address and IP management
All IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and
Alleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate
connections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration
record.

§5 TELEMETRY CONDITION FOR PERMISSION TO OPERATE
§5. ≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry.
This requirement applies to all in-scope DER sites, including aggregated facilities under
DIS-01 §3.4.
Live telemetry, for the purposes of §5, means that the RTU installed under §3 is:

a. Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;

Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).\n c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the\naggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.\n d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER\ncommissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or\ncapacity change requiring a new interconnection application.\n4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 2Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02\nWhere a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common\ncoupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the\naggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.\n§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS\n§3.1   Ownership and installation\nEach in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)\ninstalled at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,\nowned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.\nThe customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC\nservice, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU\ninstallation drawing.\n§3.3   Functional requirements\nEach RTU shall, at minimum:\n a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station\ninstrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.\n b. Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum\nof seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon\nrestoration.\n d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as\ndiagnostic points.\n e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom\nSCADA/EMS Engineering only.\n§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements\nThe RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation\ndrawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a\ndedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour\noutage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.\n§3.5   Time synchronization\nThe RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)\ntime or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a\ntimestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.\n§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification\n§3.2   Approved models\nThe utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU\nservice: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power\nplant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the\nutility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 3\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\nPrior to the RTU being accepted as commissioned, Alleniom shall perform an end-to-end\npoint-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,\nexercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.\nCommissioning of the RTU is a prerequisite to the telemetry condition stated in §5.\n§4   COMMUNICATIONS\n§4.1   Communications transport\nThe RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by\nSCADA/EMS Engineering:\n a.   Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or\n b.   Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or\n c.   Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held\nby Alleniom.\nCustomer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.\nWhere site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for\ninterconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.\n§4.2   SCADA protocol\nThe RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Configuration\nparameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —\nshall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.\n§4.3   Availability\nThe end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a\nmonthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;\n\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 4\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\n b.   Communicating with Alleniom SCADA over an approved transport (§4) at the refresh\ncadence required by §6; and\n c.   Presenting all required data points (§6) as valid (not stale, not forced, not flagged\nbad-quality) at the SCADA operator display at the moment Permission to Operate (PTO) is\nissued.\nCompliance with §5 is confirmed by the SOC Shift Supervisor on shift at the time PTO is\nrequested. PTO shall not be\nissued to any in-scope DER site until §5 is satisfied.\n§6   DATA POINTS AND REFRESH RATES\n§6.1   Required data points\nEach in-scope DER site shall present, at minimum, the following analog and status points to\nAlleniom SCADA. Where the site's arrangement includes multiple inverter blocks or multiple\naggregated facilities behind a common POI, values shall be reported both individually per block\nand as a facility total.\nAnalog values (per site, and per block where applicable):\nPoint\nUnits\nSign convention\nReal power, net export at POI\nkW\nExport positive\nReactive power, net at POI\nkVAr\nAbsorbing positive\nPOI voltage, per phase\nV\n—\nPOI current, per phase\nA\n—\nFrequency at POI\nHz\n—\nGross generation (per inverter block)\nkW\nGeneration positive\nAuxiliary/parasitic load (where separately metered)\nkW\nLoad positive\nCumulative energy delivered\nkWh\nExport positive\nCumulative energy received\nkWh\nImport positive\nAmbient / cabinet temperature (RTU health)\n°C\n—\nStatus and diagnostic points:\nPoint\nDescription\nSite online / offline\nAggregate operating state of the DER\nInverter/PCS block status\nPer block: run, standby, fault\nCommunications heartbeat\nRTU-to-SCADA path health\nTime-sync quality\nGNSS/NTP discipline status\nConfiguration version\nActive RTU configuration identifier\nAlarm summary\nRolled-up device alarm state\n§6.2   Refresh rates\n\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 5\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\nAnalog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3\nClass 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than\nevery sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an\nintegrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be\nreported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.\n§6.3   Data quality\nEvery value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,\nrestart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the\nRTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be\nreported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.\n§6.4   Retention\nAlleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six\n(36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,\nengineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.\n§7   CYBERSECURITY\n§7.1   Applicability\nThe RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any\ncustomer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this\nsection. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication\nagainst Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are\nmanaged by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.\n§7.3   Communications security\nDNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All\ncommunications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an\nAlleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates\nshall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.\n§7.4   Firmware, configuration, and change management\nRTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following\nthe Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a\ncryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or\nreconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.\n§7.5   Logging and monitoring\nThe RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,\nand firmware operations. Enclosure keys, cores, and any\nphysical access tokens are held by Alleniom. Physical intrusion of the enclosure shall generate a\nstatus point (tamper alarm) reported to SCADA under §6.\n§7.7   Incident response\nThe customer shall report, without delay, any known or suspected compromise of the RTU, its\nenclosure, its communications transport, or any interface between customer equipment and\nutility-owned telemetry equipment. Reports shall be directed to the Alleniom SOC and to\nSCADA/EMS Engineering.\n§7.8   Decommissioning\nAt end of life, the RTU and its cryptographic material are returned to Alleniom for secure disposal.\nCustomer equipment previously interfaced to the RTU shall be sanitized of any Alleniom-provided\ncredentials before it is repurposed or disposed of.\nEnd of TCS-02.","content_type":"markdown","editor":"markdown","is_published":true,"is_private":false,"locale":"en","created_at":"2026-11-27T02:27:42.791943+00:00","updated_at":"2026-11-27T02:27:42.791943+00:00","tags":["standards","telemetry"],"author_name":"Evan Solberg","author_email":"evan.solberg@alleniom.com"},"error":""}"}],"structuredContent":{"success":true,"page":{"id":48,"path":"der-program/standards/tcs-02-telemetry-comms-standard","title":"TCS-02 Telemetry Comms Standard","description":"Telemetry and Communications Standard effective 06/01/2021 requiring RTU and SCADA for sites 500 kW and above","content":"# TCS-02 Telemetry Comms Standard

FROM:	Dana Whitcomb, VP, Distribution Operations
DATE:	06/27/2025
SUBJECT:	Backlog Review — Commercial DER Interconnection Program
The Alleron Municipal League's letter of 06/20/2025, submitted on behalf of fourteen member municipalities and school districts and copied to the APUC Energy Resources Division, is the trigger. We are not going to litigate its tone. We are going to fix the underlying condition that produced it.
Effective immediately, I am ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. The scope covers the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population — every application currently sitting in the program queue. I want each one accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action.
The following non-negotiable dates govern this work:
1. 08/15/2025 — Formal written response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs owns the response letter. Harriet Ngoyi is the signatory. The response must address the League's five enumerated requests substantively and by project, not in aggregate.
2. 09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. Queue accounting must be complete before we walk into that room. I will not brief the Commission on partial data. If a project's disposition is not final by 09/10/2025, I want the reason documented in the file, not explained at the podium.
Ground rules for every disposition reached in this review:
Every disposition must be tariff-defensible. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, or operating guideline that supports the action. If the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as they are written. Do not shortcut them, and do not extend them beyond what the tariff contemplates.
Where standards or procedural conflicts exist, route them through the established referral process. Do not resolve them informally in the queue.
No interim energization, no political prioritization, and no queue-date inheritance outside of what the tariff and program policy permit.
Reporting cadence. I want weekly progress updates to the VP office, in writing, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025. Format: counts by disposition category, exceptions requiring VP attention, and any item at risk of missing the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates. Meera, Ivo, and Marcus will support the DER Program Manager with the data pulls, study status, and telemetry/equipment inputs their groups own.
Escalate obstacles to me directly. I would rather field a problem on a Tuesday than read about it in a League follow-up letter.
/s/
Dana Whitcomb
Vice President, Distribution Operations
Alleniom Utilities
